#### 4.2.5 Comment and Whitespace Scanning

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CommentScanInput
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the source scalar sequence used by comment and whitespace scanning.
-->

T = S.scalars

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

**Line Comment Scan.**

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Scan-Line-Comment
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: A line comment scan consumes from // through the next line feed or end of source.
labels: Scan-Line-Comment
-->

**(Scan-Line-Comment)**
T[i] = '/'    T[i+1] = '/'    j = min{ p | i ≤ p ∧ (p = |T| ∨ T[p] = LF) }
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ScanLineComment(T, i) ⇓ j

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.DocCommentClassification
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, documentation, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines doc comment marker/body classification and line comment token skipping.
-->

**Doc Comment Classification.**
kind = DocMarker(T, i)
body = DocBody(T, i, j)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Doc-Comment
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, documentation, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: A scanned line comment with a doc marker produces a doc comment record with kind, body, and source span.
labels: Doc-Comment
-->

**(Doc-Comment)**
Γ ⊢ ScanLineComment(T, i) ⇓ j    kind ≠ ⊥
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ DocComment(T, i) ⇓ ⟨kind, body, SpanOfText(S, i, j)⟩

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.LineCommentSkipping
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines that line comments produce no tokens and advance to the scanned line-comment end.
-->

LineCommentTokens(T, i) = []
LineCommentNext(T, i) = j where Γ ⊢ ScanLineComment(T, i) ⇓ j

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.BlockCommentState
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines nested block comment scanning states.
-->

**Block Comment Scan (Nested).**
BlockState = { BlockScan(T, i, d, i_0) | 0 ≤ i_0 ≤ i ≤ |T| ∧ d ∈ ℕ } ∪ { BlockDone(j) | 0 ≤ j ≤ |T| }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Block-Start
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Nested block comment scanning increments depth when an opening block-comment delimiter is encountered.
labels: Block-Start
-->

**(Block-Start)**
T[i] = '/'    T[i+1] = '*'
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨BlockScan(T, i, d, i_0)⟩ → ⟨BlockScan(T, i+2, d+1, i_0)⟩

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Block-End
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Nested block comment scanning decrements depth when a closing delimiter is encountered above depth one.
labels: Block-End
-->

**(Block-End)**
T[i] = '*'    T[i+1] = '/'    d > 1
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨BlockScan(T, i, d, i_0)⟩ → ⟨BlockScan(T, i+2, d-1, i_0)⟩

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Block-Done
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Nested block comment scanning completes when a closing delimiter is encountered at depth one.
labels: Block-Done
-->

**(Block-Done)**
T[i] = '*'    T[i+1] = '/'    d = 1
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨BlockScan(T, i, d, i_0)⟩ → ⟨BlockDone(i+2)⟩

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Block-Step
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Nested block comment scanning advances one scalar when neither opening nor closing delimiter starts at the current position.
labels: Block-Step
-->

**(Block-Step)**
T[i..i+2] ≠ "/*"    T[i..i+2] ≠ "*/"
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨BlockScan(T, i, d, i_0)⟩ → ⟨BlockScan(T, i+1, d, i_0)⟩

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Block-Comment-Unterminated
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.comments
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Unterminated nested block comments emit the block-comment-unterminated diagnostic at the opening delimiter.
labels: Block-Comment-Unterminated
-->

**(Block-Comment-Unterminated)**
⟨BlockScan(T, i, d, i_0)⟩ →* ⟨BlockScan(T, |T|, d, i_0)⟩    d > 0    c = Code(Block-Comment-Unterminated)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ Emit(c, SpanOfText(S, i_0, i_0+2))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 4.2.6 Literal Lexing

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.LiteralLexingInput
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the source scalar sequence used by literal lexing.
-->

T = S.scalars

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

**Syntax.**

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.LiteralLexing
kind: grammar
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, parser, diagnostics, oracle.grammar, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines integer, float, string, character, boolean, and null literal lexical grammar and token formation requirements for quoted literals.
-->

```ebnf
integer_literal  ::= (decimal_integer | hex_integer | octal_integer | binary_integer) int_suffix?
decimal_integer  ::= dec_digit ("_"* dec_digit)*
hex_integer      ::= "0x" hex_digit ("_"* hex_digit)*
octal_integer    ::= "0o" oct_digit ("_"* oct_digit)*
binary_integer   ::= "0b" bin_digit ("_"* bin_digit)*
int_suffix       ::= "i8" | "i16" | "i32" | "i64" | "i128" | "u8" | "u16" | "u32" | "u64" | "u128" | "isize" | "usize"

float_literal ::= decimal_integer "." decimal_integer? exponent? float_suffix?
exponent      ::= ("e" | "E") ("+" | "-")? decimal_integer
float_suffix  ::= "f" | "f16" | "f32" | "f64"

string_literal   ::= '"' (string_char | escape_sequence)* '"'
string_char      ::= string_char_unit
escape_sequence  ::= "\n" | "\r" | "\t" | "\\" | "\"" | "\'" | "\0" | "\x" hex_digit hex_digit | "\u{" hex_digit+ "}"

char_literal ::= "'" (char_content | escape_sequence) "'"
char_content ::= char_content_unit

The productions `string_literal` and `char_literal` define well-formed quoted literal spellings. During tokenization, any terminated quoted span with the corresponding delimiter MUST form a `StringLiteral` or `CharLiteral` token even when its interior is ill-formed. Bad escapes and invalid character-literal contents MUST emit their corresponding diagnostics and MUST NOT suppress token formation. Unterminated quoted spans are excluded from token formation and follow the recovery rules in §4.2.11.

bool_literal ::= "true" | "false"
null_literal ::= "null"
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.FloatSuffixDefaulting
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, type-checker, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines float literal suffix omission, inferred-width suffix f, explicit-width suffixes, default f32 behavior, expected-type checking, and conflicting explicit-width errors.
-->

**Float Suffix and Defaulting.**
Float literals MAY omit a suffix when they contain a decimal point. The suffix `f` indicates a float literal with width inferred from context; explicit suffixes `f16`, `f32`, `f64` specify the width directly. If no expected type is present, an unsuffixed decimal float literal defaults to `f32`. If an expected or declared float type is present, that expected type governs checking of unsuffixed and `f`-suffixed literals. Using an explicit width suffix with a conflicting expected type is an error.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.SimpleEscape
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Simple escape set and validity relation
-->

**Escape Validity.**
SimpleEscape = {`\\`, `\"`, `\'`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\0`}
EscapeOk(`\\`) ∧ EscapeOk(`\"`) ∧ EscapeOk(`\'`) ∧ EscapeOk(`\n`) ∧ EscapeOk(`\r`) ∧ EscapeOk(`\t`) ∧ EscapeOk(`\0`)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ByteEscapeValidity
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Byte escape validity relation
-->

EscapeOk("\\x" h_1 h_2) ⇔ HexDigit(h_1) ∧ HexDigit(h_2)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.UnicodeEscapeValidity
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Unicode escape validity relation
-->

EscapeOk("\\u{" h_1 … h_n "}") ⇔ 1 ≤ n ≤ 6 ∧ UnicodeScalar(HexValue(h_1 … h_n))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.StringCharacterValidity
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: String literal character validity relation
-->

StringChar(c) ⇔ UnicodeScalar(c) ∧ c ≠ "\"" ∧ c ≠ "\\" ∧ c ≠ U+000A

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CharacterLiteralContentValidity
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Character literal content validity relation
-->

CharContent(c) ⇔ UnicodeScalar(c) ∧ c ≠ "'" ∧ c ≠ "\\" ∧ c ≠ U+000A

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.QuotedLiteralCharacterUnits
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Quoted literal grammar character-unit sets
-->

string_char_unit = { c | StringChar(c) }
char_content_unit = { c | CharContent(c) }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericSuffixSets
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Numeric literal base prefixes and suffix sets
-->

**Underscore Constraints.**
BasePrefix = {"0x", "0o", "0b"}
IntSuffixSet = {"i8", "i16", "i32", "i64", "i128", "u8", "u16", "u32", "u64", "u128", "isize", "usize"}
FloatSuffixSet = {"f", "f16", "f32", "f64"}
NumSuffix = IntSuffixSet ∪ FloatSuffixSet

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.StringHelpers
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: String helper functions used by literal scanning
-->

At(s, i) = s[i]
StartsWith(s, p) ⇔ s[0..|p|) = p
EndsWith(s, p) ⇔ s[|s| - |p|..|s|) = p
Remove(s, c) = [ s[i] | 0 ≤ i < |s| ∧ s[i] ≠ c ]
Concat([]) = `"\""`
Concat([s]) = s
Concat(s::ss) = s ++ Concat(ss)    (|ss| > 0)
Hex2(b) = HexDigit(⌊b/16⌋) ++ HexDigit(b mod 16)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.HexDigitValue
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Hexadecimal digit value relation
-->

HexDigitValue(`'0'`) = 0    HexDigitValue(`'1'`) = 1    HexDigitValue(`'2'`) = 2    HexDigitValue(`'3'`) = 3    HexDigitValue(`'4'`) = 4    HexDigitValue(`'5'`) = 5    HexDigitValue(`'6'`) = 6    HexDigitValue(`'7'`) = 7    HexDigitValue(`'8'`) = 8    HexDigitValue(`'9'`) = 9
HexDigitValue(`'a'`) = 10    HexDigitValue(`'b'`) = 11    HexDigitValue(`'c'`) = 12    HexDigitValue(`'d'`) = 13    HexDigitValue(`'e'`) = 14    HexDigitValue(`'f'`) = 15
HexDigitValue(`'A'`) = 10    HexDigitValue(`'B'`) = 11    HexDigitValue(`'C'`) = 12    HexDigitValue(`'D'`) = 13    HexDigitValue(`'E'`) = 14    HexDigitValue(`'F'`) = 15
HexValue(h_1…h_n) = ∑_{k=1}^{n} HexDigitValue(h_k) · 16^(n-k)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.DecimalDigitValue
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Decimal digit value relation
-->

DecDigitValue(`'0'`) = 0    DecDigitValue(`'1'`) = 1    DecDigitValue(`'2'`) = 2    DecDigitValue(`'3'`) = 3    DecDigitValue(`'4'`) = 4    DecDigitValue(`'5'`) = 5    DecDigitValue(`'6'`) = 6    DecDigitValue(`'7'`) = 7    DecDigitValue(`'8'`) = 8    DecDigitValue(`'9'`) = 9

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.OctalDigitValue
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Octal digit value relation
-->

OctDigitValue(`'0'`) = 0    OctDigitValue(`'1'`) = 1    OctDigitValue(`'2'`) = 2    OctDigitValue(`'3'`) = 3    OctDigitValue(`'4'`) = 4    OctDigitValue(`'5'`) = 5    OctDigitValue(`'6'`) = 6    OctDigitValue(`'7'`) = 7

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.BinaryDigitValue
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Binary digit value relation
-->

BinDigitValue(`'0'`) = 0    BinDigitValue(`'1'`) = 1

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericValues
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Decimal, octal, and binary numeric value relations
-->

DecValue(d_1…d_n) = ∑_{k=1}^{n} DecDigitValue(d_k) · 10^(n-k)
OctValue(d_1…d_n) = ∑_{k=1}^{n} OctDigitValue(d_k) · 8^(n-k)
BinValue(d_1…d_n) = ∑_{k=1}^{n} BinDigitValue(d_k) · 2^(n-k)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericUnderscorePredicates
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Numeric literal underscore validity predicates
-->

StartsWithUnderscore(s) ⇔ At(s, 0) = "_"
EndsWithUnderscore(s) ⇔ At(s, |s|-1) = "_"
AfterBasePrefixUnderscore(s) ⇔ ∃ p ∈ BasePrefix. StartsWith(s, Concat(p, "_"))
ExponentMarker(s, i) ⇔ (∀ p ∈ BasePrefix. ¬ StartsWith(s, p)) ∧ At(s, i) ∈ {"e", "E"}
AdjacentExponentUnderscore(s) ⇔ ∃ i. At(s, i) = "_" ∧ ((i > 0 ∧ ExponentMarker(s, i-1)) ∨ (i+1 < |s| ∧ ExponentMarker(s, i+1)))
BeforeSuffixUnderscore(s) ⇔ ∃ suf ∈ NumSuffix. EndsWith(s, Concat("_", suf))
NumericUnderscoreOk(s) ⇔ ¬ StartsWithUnderscore(s) ∧ ¬ EndsWithUnderscore(s) ∧ ¬ AfterBasePrefixUnderscore(s) ∧ ¬ AdjacentExponentUnderscore(s) ∧ ¬ BeforeSuffixUnderscore(s)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericDigitRuns
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Maximal-prefix numeric digit run scanners
-->

**Numeric Scan (Maximal Prefix).**
DecRun(T, i) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ ∀ k ∈ [i, j). (DecDigit(T[k]) ∨ T[k] = "_") })
HexRun(T, i) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ ∀ k ∈ [i, j). (HexDigit(T[k]) ∨ T[k] = "_") })
OctRun(T, i) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ ∀ k ∈ [i, j). (OctDigit(T[k]) ∨ T[k] = "_") })
BinRun(T, i) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ ∀ k ∈ [i, j). (BinDigit(T[k]) ∨ T[k] = "_") })

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.SuffixMatch
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Maximal suffix match scanner
-->

SuffixMatch(T, i, U) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ Lexeme(T, i, j) ∈ U })

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ExponentScan
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Numeric exponent scanner
-->

ExpSignEnd(T, i) =
 i+1  if i < |T| ∧ T[i] ∈ {"+", "-"}
 i    otherwise

ExpEnd(T, i) =
 DecRun(T, ExpSignEnd(T, i+1))  if i < |T| ∧ T[i] ∈ {"e", "E"}
 i                              otherwise

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.DecCoreEnd
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Decimal numeric core scanner with float/range disambiguation
-->

DecCoreEnd(T, i) =
 ExpEnd(T, q)  if p = DecRun(T, i) ∧ p < |T| ∧ T[p] = "." ∧ (p+1 ≥ |T| ∨ T[p+1] ≠ ".") ∧ q = DecRun(T, p+1)
 ExpEnd(T, p)  if p = DecRun(T, i) ∧ (p ≥ |T| ∨ T[p] ≠ "." ∨ (p+1 < |T| ∧ T[p+1] = "."))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.DecimalRangeNoFloatCore
kind: normative-requirement
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, parser, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Decimal runs immediately followed by range operators do not form float cores.
-->

A decimal run immediately followed by `..` or `..=` MUST NOT form a float core. In that case `DecCoreEnd(T, i) = DecRun(T, i)`, and the following `.` remains available to operator tokenization.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericCoreEnd
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Numeric literal core scanner
-->

NumericCoreEnd(T, i) =
 HexRun(T, i+2)  if T[i..i+2] = "0x"
 OctRun(T, i+2)  if T[i..i+2] = "0o"
 BinRun(T, i+2)  if T[i..i+2] = "0b"
 DecCoreEnd(T, i)  otherwise

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericScanEnd
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Numeric literal scan end relation
-->

NumericScanEnd(T, i) = SuffixMatch(T, NumericCoreEnd(T, i), NumSuffix)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericFloatCorePredicates
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Numeric literal dot, exponent, and float-core predicates
-->

HasDot(T, i, j) ⇔ ∃ p. i ≤ p < j ∧ T[p] = "."
HasExp(T, i, j) ⇔ ∃ p. i ≤ p < j ∧ T[p] ∈ {"e", "E"}
HasFloatCore(T, i, j) ⇔ HasDot(T, i, j)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericKind
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Numeric literal kind selection
-->

NumericKind(T, i) =
 FloatLiteral  if HasFloatCore(T, i, NumericCoreEnd(T, i))
 IntLiteral    otherwise

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Lex-Int
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Integer literal lexing succeeds for a decimal-starting numeric scan whose numeric kind is IntLiteral.
labels: Lex-Int
-->

**(Lex-Int)**
DecDigit(T[i])    j = NumericScanEnd(T, i)    NumericKind(T, i) = IntLiteral
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ IntLiteral(T, i) ⇓ j

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Lex-Float
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Float literal lexing succeeds for a decimal-starting numeric scan whose numeric kind is FloatLiteral.
labels: Lex-Float
-->

**(Lex-Float)**
DecDigit(T[i])    j = NumericScanEnd(T, i)    NumericKind(T, i) = FloatLiteral
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ FloatLiteral(T, i) ⇓ j

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.NumericLexemeValidation
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines valid and invalid numeric lexeme predicates using literal grammar and underscore constraints.
-->

NumericLexemeOk(T, i, j) ⇔ (Lexeme(T, i, j) matches integer_literal ∨ Lexeme(T, i, j) matches float_literal) ∧ NumericUnderscoreOk(Lexeme(T, i, j))
NumericLexemeBad(T, i, j) ⇔ ¬ NumericLexemeOk(T, i, j)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Lex-Numeric-Err
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Malformed numeric lexemes emit the numeric literal diagnostic at the scanned numeric span.
labels: Lex-Numeric-Err
-->

**(Lex-Numeric-Err)**
DecDigit(T[i])    j = NumericScanEnd(T, i)    NumericLexemeBad(T, i, j)    c = Code(Lex-Numeric-Err)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ Emit(c, SpanOfText(S, i, j))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.DecimalLeadingZeros
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines decimal leading-zero detection for numeric literal warnings.
-->

**Leading Zeros.**
Digits(s) = Remove(s, "_")
DecimalLeadingZero(T, i, j) ⇔ Lexeme(T, i, j) matches decimal_integer ∧ |Digits(Lexeme(T, i, j))| > 1 ∧ At(Digits(Lexeme(T, i, j)), 0) = '0'

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Warn-DecimalLeadingZero
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required

applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Decimal literals with leading zeros emit W-SRC-0301 over the literal span.
labels: Warn-DecimalLeadingZero
-->

DecimalLeadingZero(T, i, j)
──────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ Emit(W-SRC-0301, SpanOfText(S, i, j))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.EscapeSequences
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines escape-sequence runtime values for simple, byte, and Unicode escapes.
-->

**EscapeSequences.**
EscapeValue(`\\`) = 0x5C
EscapeValue(`\"`) = 0x22
EscapeValue(`\'`) = 0x27
EscapeValue(`\n`) = 0x0A
EscapeValue(`\r`) = 0x0D
EscapeValue(`\t`) = 0x09
EscapeValue(`\0`) = 0x00
EscapeValue("\\x" h_1 h_2) = HexValue(h_1 h_2)
EscapeValue("\\u{" h_1 … h_n "}") = EncodeUTF8(HexValue(h_1 … h_n))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Lex-String
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: String literal lexing succeeds when a quote starts a terminated string span.
labels: Lex-String
-->

**(Lex-String)**
T[i] = "\""    StringTerminator(T, i) = q    q < |T|    T[q] = "\""
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ StringLiteral(T, i) ⇓ q + 1

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.BackslashCount
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Backslash count helper for quoted literals
-->

BackslashCount(T, p) = max{ k | 0 ≤ k ≤ p ∧ ∀ r ∈ [p-k, p). T[r] = "\\" }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.StringTerminator
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: String literal terminator detection
-->

UnescapedQuote(T, p) ⇔ T[p] = "\"" ∧ BackslashCount(T, p) mod 2 = 0
StringTerminator(T, i) = min{ q | q > i ∧ (UnescapedQuote(T, q) ∨ T[q] = LF ∨ q = |T|) }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.LineFeedOrEOFBeforeClose
kind: formal-definition

strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Unterminated quoted literal predicate
-->

LineFeedOrEOFBeforeClose(T, i) ⇔ StringTerminator(T, i) = |T| ∨ T[StringTerminator(T, i)] = LF

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Escape-sequence match relation
-->

EscapeMatch(T, p, q) ⇔ Lexeme(T, p, q) matches escape_sequence ∧ EscapeOk(Lexeme(T, p, q))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Bad escape predicate
-->

BadEscapeAt(T, p) ⇔ T[p] = "\\" ∧ ¬ ∃ q. EscapeMatch(T, p, q)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

owner: lexer.literals

-->

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

-->

**(Lex-String-Unterminated)**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ Emit(c, SpanOfText(S, i, i+1))

-->

UnescapedApostrophe(T, p) ⇔ T[p] = "'" ∧ BackslashCount(T, p) mod 2 = 0

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CharacterLiteralInvalid
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, type-checker, abi, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Character literal invalidity predicate
-->

CharLiteralInvalid(T, i) ⇔ CharScalarCount(T, i) ≠ 1

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CharacterScalarCount
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.literals
applies-to: lexer, type-checker, abi, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Character literal scalar-count relation
-->

CharScalarCountFrom(T, p, q) = 0 ⇔ p ≥ q
CharScalarCountFrom(T, p, q) = 1 + CharScalarCountFrom(T, p+1, q) ⇔ p < q ∧ T[p] ≠ "\\"
CharScalarCountFrom(T, p, q) = 1 + CharScalarCountFrom(T, r, q) ⇔ p < q ∧ T[p] = "\\" ∧ EscapeMatch(T, p, r)
CharScalarCountFrom(T, p, q) = 1 + CharScalarCountFrom(T, p+1, q) ⇔ p < q ∧ T[p] = "\\" ∧ ¬ ∃ r. EscapeMatch(T, p, r)
CharScalarCount(T, i) = CharScalarCountFrom(T, i+1, CharTerminator(T, i))

**Literal Tokenization Helpers.**

#### 4.2.8 Operator and Punctuator Lexing

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.OperatorPunctuatorSets
kind: formal-definition

owner: lexer.operators

OpSet = OperatorSet
PuncSet = PunctuatorSet

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.operators
applies-to: lexer, parser, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Operator and punctuator match relations
-->

OpMatch(T, i) = { (o, j) | o ∈ OpSet ∧ Lexeme(T, i, j) = o }
PuncMatch(T, i) = { (p, j) | p ∈ PuncSet ∧ Lexeme(T, i, j) = p }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

OpTok(T, i) = { (Operator(o), j) | (o, j) ∈ OpMatch(T, i) }
PuncTok(T, i) = { (Punctuator(p), j) | (p, j) ∈ PuncMatch(T, i) }

#### 4.2.9 Maximal-Munch Rule

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.MaximalMunchInput
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.maximal-munch
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Maximal-munch input scalar sequence
-->

T = S.scalars

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.IsQuote
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.maximal-munch
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Quoted-literal start predicate
-->

IsQuote(c) ⇔ c ∈ {"\"", "'"}

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TokenCandidates
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.maximal-munch
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Token candidate selection relation
-->

Candidates(T, i) =
 StringTok(T, i) ∪ CharTok(T, i)  if IsQuote(T[i])
 FloatTok(T, i) ∪ IntTok(T, i)    if DecDigit(T[i])
 IdentToken(T, i)                 if IdentStart(T[i])
 OpTok(T, i) ∪ PuncTok(T, i)      if OpTok(T, i) ≠ ∅ ∨ PuncTok(T, i) ≠ ∅
 ∅                                otherwise

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.LongestCandidates
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.maximal-munch
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Longest token candidate relation
-->

Longest(C) = { (k, j) ∈ C | ∀ (k', j') ∈ C, j ≥ j' }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.KindPriority
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.maximal-munch
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Token kind priority relation for maximal-munch tie-breaking
-->

KindPriority(IntLiteral) = 3
KindPriority(FloatLiteral) = 3
KindPriority(StringLiteral) = 3
KindPriority(CharLiteral) = 3
KindPriority(BoolLiteral) = 3
KindPriority(NullLiteral) = 3
KindPriority(Identifier) = 2
KindPriority(Keyword(_)) = 2
KindPriority(Operator(_)) = 1
KindPriority(Punctuator(_)) = 0

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.PickLongest
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.maximal-munch
applies-to: lexer, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Longest-token selection relation
-->

PickLongest(C) = argmax_{(k, j) ∈ C} ⟨j, KindPriority(k)⟩

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Max-Munch
kind: formal-rule
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.maximal-munch
applies-to: lexer, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Next-token lexing succeeds by choosing the longest candidate with token-kind priority tie-breaking.
labels: Max-Munch
-->

**(Max-Munch)**
PickLongest(C) = (k, j)
──────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ NextToken(T, i) ⇓ (k, j)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-rule

**(Max-Munch-Err)**
Candidates(T, i) = ∅    c = Code(Max-Munch-Err)
────────────────────────────────────────────────

GenericCloseException = false

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-definition

T = S.scalars

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.LiteralAndCommentRanges
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.security
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines literal and comment range predicates and inside-literal-or-comment detection.
-->

**Literal and Comment Ranges.**
LineCommentRange(T, i, j) ⇔ Γ ⊢ ScanLineComment(T, i) ⇓ j
BlockCommentRange(T, i, j) ⇔ T[i..i+2] = "/*" ∧ ⟨BlockScan(T, i, 0, i)⟩ →* ⟨BlockDone(j)⟩
StringRange(T, i, j) ⇔ Γ ⊢ StringLiteral(T, i) ⇓ j
CharRange(T, i, j) ⇔ Γ ⊢ CharLiteral(T, i) ⇓ j
InsideLiteralOrComment(i) ⇔ ∃ a, b. a ≤ i < b ∧ (LineCommentRange(T, a, b) ∨ BlockCommentRange(T, a, b) ∨ StringRange(T, a, b) ∨ CharRange(T, a, b))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

strength: required

applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines sensitive Unicode scalar positions within a source span.
-->

**Sensitive Positions in a Span.**
SensitiveInSpan(T, i, j) = [ p | i ≤ p < j ∧ Sensitive(T[p]) ]

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.UnsafeTokenSpans
kind: formal-definition
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.security
applies-to: lexer, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines token-only unsafe span detection through brace matching and span construction.
-->

**Unsafe Spans (Token-Only).**
IsLBrace(t) ⇔ t.kind = Punctuator("{")
IsRBrace(t) ⇔ t.kind = Punctuator("}")

NextNonNewline(K, i) = ⊥ ⇔ { j | j ≥ i ∧ K[j].kind ≠ Newline } = ∅
NextNonNewline(K, i) = j ⇔ j = min{ j | j ≥ i ∧ K[j].kind ≠ Newline }

MatchBrace(K, j) = min{ k | k > j ∧ Balance(j, k) = 0 ∧ ∀ m ∈ (j, k), Balance(j, m) > 0 }

Balance(K, j, m) = |{ x | j ≤ x ≤ m ∧ IsLBrace(K[x]) }| - |{ x | j ≤ x ≤ m ∧ IsRBrace(K[x]) }|
MatchBrace(K, j) = ⊥ ⇔ { k | k > j ∧ Balance(K, j, k) = 0 ∧ ∀ m ∈ (j, k). Balance(K, j, m) > 0 } = ∅

SpanFrom(t_a, t_b) = ⟨t_a.span.file, t_a.span.start_offset, t_b.span.end_offset, t_a.span.start_line, t_a.span.start_col, t_b.span.end_line, t_b.span.end_col⟩

UnsafeSpans(K) = { SpanFrom(K[j], K[k]) | K[i].kind = Keyword("unsafe"), j = NextNonNewline(K, i+1), K[j].kind = Punctuator("{"), k = MatchBrace(K, j), k ≠ ⊥ }

UnsafeAtByte(b) ⇔ ∃ sp ∈ UnsafeSpans(K). b ∈ SpanRange(sp)

UnsafeSpanMode = TokenOnly

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

strength: required

**Lexical Security Check.**
Sens = [ p | Sensitive(T[p]) ∧ ¬ InsideLiteralOrComment(p) ]

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.TupleProjectionLexicalDisambiguation
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: lexical
strength: required
owner: lexer.tokenization
applies-to: lexer, parser, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires tuple projection integer-token precedence over a decimal-float token immediately after an emitted dot token.
-->

**Tuple Projection Lexical Disambiguation.**
The postfix form `postfix_expr "." int_literal` takes precedence over a decimal-float token that would begin immediately after an already-emitted `.` token. If the most recently emitted token in `K` has lexeme `"."`, and the source at `i` admits both an `IntLiteral` token ending at `j_i` and a `FloatLiteral` token ending at `j_f` with `j_i < j_f`, the lexer MUST emit the `IntLiteral` token over `[i, j_i)` and continue from `j_i`. The following `.` remains available for subsequent tokenization.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

⟨LexScan(S, i, K, D, Sens)⟩ → ⟨LexError(c)⟩

| `E-SRC-0104` | Error    | Compile-time | Forbidden control character or null byte                     |
| `E-SRC-0301` | Error    | Compile-time | Unterminated string literal                                  |
| `E-SRC-0302` | Error    | Compile-time | Invalid escape sequence                                      |
| `E-SRC-0303` | Error    | Compile-time | Invalid character literal                                    |
| `E-SRC-0304` | Error    | Compile-time | Malformed numeric literal                                    |
| `E-SRC-0306` | Error    | Compile-time | Unterminated block comment                                   |
| `E-SRC-0307` | Error    | Compile-time | Invalid Unicode in identifier                                |
| `E-SRC-0308` | Error    | Compile-time | Lexically sensitive Unicode character outside `unsafe` block |
| `E-SRC-0309` | Error    | Compile-time | Tokenization failed to classify a character sequence         |
| `E-SRC-0310` | Error    | Compile-time | Confusable identifier pair                                   |
| `E-SRC-0311` | Error    | Compile-time | Mixed-script identifier                                      |
| `W-SRC-0101` | Warning  | Compile-time | UTF-8 BOM present at the start of the file                   |
| `W-SRC-0301` | Warning  | Compile-time | Leading zeros in decimal literal                             |
| `W-SRC-0308` | Warning  | Compile-time | Lexically sensitive Unicode character within `unsafe` block  |

### 5.2 AST Meta-Conventions

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ASTNodeUniverse
kind: formal-definition

strength: required
owner: parser.ast
applies-to: parser, ast, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the AST node universe and node accessor domains.
-->

ASTNode = ASTItem ∪ ASTExpr ∪ ASTPattern ∪ ASTType ∪ ASTStmt
SpanOfNode : ASTNode → Span
DocOf : ASTNode → (DocList ∪ {⊥})

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ASTParseCtorDefaults
kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.ast
applies-to: parser, ast, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines span/doc defaults and parse-constructor field filling.
-->

SpanDefault(P, P') = SpanBetween(P, P')
DocDefault = []
DocOptDefault = ⊥
FillSpan(n, P, P') =
 n[span := SpanDefault(P, P')]  if SpanMissing(n)
 n                             otherwise
FillDoc(n) =
 n[doc := DocDefault]  if DocMissing(n)
 n                     otherwise
FillDocOpt(n) =
 n[doc_opt := DocOptDefault]  if DocOptMissing(n)
 n                            otherwise
ParseCtor(n, P, P') = FillDocOpt(FillDoc(FillSpan(n, P, P')))

Advance(P) = ⟨K, i+1, D, j, d, Δ⟩
Clone(P) = ⟨K, i, D, j, d, []⟩
MergeDiag(P_b, P_d, P_s) = ⟨TokStream(P_s), TokIndex(P_s), DocStream(P_s), DocIndex(P_s), Depth(P_s), DiagStream(P_b) ++ DiagStream(P_d)⟩

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ParserSpanBetween
kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.state
applies-to: parser, ast, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines consumed-token and span construction between parser states.
-->

LastConsumed(P, P') =
 K[i'-1]  if i' > i
 Tok(P)   if i' = i

SpanBetween(P, P') = SpanFrom(Tok(P), LastConsumed(P, P'))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.SplitSpan2
kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.state
applies-to: parser, ast, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines two-token span splitting for a two-character token span.
-->

SplitSpan2(sp) = (sp_L, sp_R) where
 sp_L.file = sp.file ∧ sp_R.file = sp.file
 sp_L.start_offset = sp.start_offset ∧ sp_L.end_offset = sp.start_offset + 1
 sp_R.start_offset = sp.start_offset + 1 ∧ sp_R.end_offset = sp.start_offset + 2
 sp_L.start_line = sp.start_line ∧ sp_L.end_line = sp.start_line
 sp_R.start_line = sp.start_line ∧ sp_R.end_line = sp.start_line
 sp_L.start_col = sp.start_col ∧ sp_L.end_col = sp.start_col + 1
 sp_R.start_col = sp.start_col + 1 ∧ sp_R.end_col = sp.start_col + 2

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.SplitShiftR
kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.state
applies-to: parser, ast, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines splitting the current shift-right operator token into two greater-than operator tokens.
-->

SplitShiftR(P) = ⟨K', i, D, j, d, Δ⟩
where Tok(P) = ⟨Operator(">>"), ">>", sp⟩ ∧ (sp_L, sp_R) = SplitSpan2(sp)
K' = K[0..i) ++ [⟨Operator(">"), ">", sp_L⟩, ⟨Operator(">"), ">", sp_R⟩] ++ K[i+1..]

IsIdent(t) ⇔ t.kind = Identifier

CtxKeyword = {"in", "key", "wait"}
Ctx(t, s) ⇔ IsIdent(t) ∧ Lexeme(t) = s ∧ s ∈ CtxKeyword

FixedIdent_Key = {"read", "write", "release", "speculative", "ordered"}

FixedIdent_Spawn = {"name", "affinity", "priority"}
FixedIdent_Dispatch = {"reduce", "ordered", "chunk", "workgroup", "min", "max", "and", "or"}
FixedIdent_Meta = {"pattern", "target", "requires", "emits"}
FixedIdent = FixedIdent_Key ∪ FixedIdent_Parallel ∪ FixedIdent_Spawn ∪ FixedIdent_Dispatch ∪ FixedIdent_Meta

## 6. Abstract Machine, Objects, Responsibility, and Authority

### 6.1 Authority Model

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.NoAmbientAuthorityDiscipline
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.model
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Establishes that observable external effects require explicit possession and use of capability values.
-->

The language adopts a no ambient authority discipline: observable external effects are possible only through explicit possession and use of capability values.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 6.1.1 Capability Universe

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CapabilityClass
kind: formal-definition
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.capabilities
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the intrinsic capability class universe.
-->

CapabilityClass = {IO, Network, HeapAllocator, Reactor, ExecutionDomain, System, Time, MonotonicTime, WallTime}

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CapInTypeSignature
kind: formal-definition
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.capabilities
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines CapInType as capability-class extraction from types.
-->

CapInType : Type → 𝒫(CapabilityClass)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CapInTypeRootMappings
kind: formal-definition
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.capabilities
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines CapInType mappings for built-in capability root types.
-->

CapInType(TypePath([`Context`])) = {IO, Network, HeapAllocator, Reactor, ExecutionDomain, System, Time}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`IO`])) = {IO}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`Network`])) = {Network}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`HeapAllocator`])) = {HeapAllocator}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`Reactor`])) = {Reactor}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`ExecutionDomain`])) = {ExecutionDomain}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`System`])) = {System}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`Time`])) = {Time}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`MonotonicTime`])) = {MonotonicTime}
CapInType(TypeDynamic([`WallTime`])) = {WallTime}

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CapInTypePermission
kind: formal-definition
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.capabilities
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines capability extraction through permission-qualified types.
-->

CapInType(TypePerm(_, T)) = CapInType(T)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CapInTypeStructuralCollections
kind: formal-definition
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.capabilities
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines capability extraction over tuple, array, and slice type components.
-->

CapInType(TypeTuple(Ts)) = ⋃{CapInType(T) | T ∈ Ts}
CapInType(TypeArray(T, _)) = CapInType(T)
CapInType(TypeSlice(T)) = CapInType(T)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CapInTypeStructuralNominal
kind: formal-definition
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.capabilities
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines structural capability extraction over compound nominal, modal, union, and applied types after alias expansion.
-->

<!-- Source: "CapInType(TypeStruct(_), TypeRecord(_), TypeUnion(_), TypeEnum(_), TypeModalState(_), TypeApply(_), …) distributes structurally over the immediate component types of the type constructor (after alias expansion)." -->
CapInType(T) distributes structurally over compound nominal, modal, union, and applied types after alias expansion.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.CapInTypeLeastFixedPointAllowed
kind: normative-requirement
phase: static-semantics
strength: optional
owner: authority.capabilities
applies-to: type-checker, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Allows implementations to compute CapInType by least fixed point over nominal and alias expansion.
-->

Implementations MAY compute `CapInType` by least fixed-point over nominal and alias expansion.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.CapInTypeCyclesTerminate
kind: normative-requirement
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.capabilities
applies-to: type-checker, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires cyclic nominal or alias expansion in CapInType computation to terminate.
-->

Cycles MUST terminate by memoization or an equivalent visited-node strategy.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 6.1.2 No Ambient Authority Requirements

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: NAA-1
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.no-ambient-authority
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Forbids implicit or global bindings whose types carry capabilities.
labels: NAA-1
-->

**(NAA-1) No implicit capability roots.** A conforming implementation MUST NOT provide any implicit or global binding whose type is capability-bearing under `CapInType`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: NAA-2
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: authority.no-ambient-authority
applies-to: runtime, entrypoints, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires Context to be the only abstract-machine capability root carrier and restricts how roots enter executable and hosted-library sessions.
labels: NAA-2
-->

**(NAA-2) Context as the sole explicit root carrier.** The only capability roots introduced by the abstract machine at runtime are those contained in `Context` values produced by `ContextInitSigma` in §24.4.5 or by `HostSessionInitSigma` in §24.4.4. A conforming implementation MUST introduce those roots only through the executable entry procedure or a hosted-library session created by the sanctioned hosted-library lifecycle.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: NAA-3
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.no-ambient-authority
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires externally observable effects to arise only from runtime host primitives or built-in procedures/methods on capability values.
labels: NAA-3
-->

**(NAA-3) Effect gating.** Any externally observable effect specified by this document MUST occur only as a consequence of calling:
- a runtime host primitive classified in §6.2, or
- a built-in procedure or method whose receiver is a capability value.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CapReq
kind: formal-definition
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.no-ambient-authority
applies-to: type-checker, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the capability requirement set for a declaration from parameter and receiver types.
-->

CapReq(d) = ⋃{CapInType(T_i) | T_i is the type of a parameter or receiver of declaration d}

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.DirectCallCapabilityInclusion
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: static-semantics
strength: required
owner: authority.no-ambient-authority
applies-to: type-checker, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Rejects direct calls whose target capability requirements are not included in the source declaration capability requirements.
-->

For every direct call from `d_src` to `d_tgt`, a conforming implementation MUST reject the program unless `CapReq(d_tgt) ⊆ CapReq(d_src)`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 6.1.3 Attenuation Requirements

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.AttenuationOperations
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: authority.attenuation
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the operations classified as authority attenuation operations.
-->

The following operations are attenuation operations:
- `$IO::restrict(root)`
- `$Network::restrict_to_host(host)`
- `$HeapAllocator::with_quota(bytes)`
- `CancelToken@Active::child()`
- `Context::cpu()`
- `Context::gpu()`
- `Context::inline()`
- `$Time::monotonic()`
- `$Time::wall()`
- `$MonotonicTime::coarsen(resolution)`
- `$WallTime::coarsen(resolution)`

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AttenuationMonotoneAuthority
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: authority.attenuation
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires derived capabilities to grant no authority beyond their source capabilities.
-->

A conforming implementation MUST ensure attenuation is monotone: a derived capability MUST NOT grant authority beyond the source capability from which it was derived.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AttenuationChildLiveness
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: authority.attenuation
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires child capabilities produced by attenuation to remain operational only while their parent capability remains live.
-->

For every attenuation operation `ChildCap = ParentCap~>attenuate(...)`, a conforming implementation MUST enforce all of the following:

- `ChildCap` remains operational only while `ParentCap` remains live.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AttenuationChildDropDoesNotDiminishParent
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: authority.attenuation
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires dropping an attenuated child capability not to invalidate or diminish its parent capability.
-->

- Dropping `ChildCap` MUST NOT invalidate or diminish `ParentCap`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AttenuationParentDropRejectedWithLiveChildren
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: authority.attenuation
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Rejects dropping a parent capability while any derived child capability remains live.
-->

- Dropping `ParentCap` while any derived child capability remains live is ill-formed.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AttenuationDelegationSubsetRouting
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: authority.attenuation
applies-to: runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires runtime delegation by an attenuated child capability to route through an equal-or-stricter authority subset.
-->

- Any runtime delegation performed by `ChildCap` MUST be routed through `ParentCap` or through an equivalent runtime object that enforces an equal-or-stricter authority subset.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 6.1.4 Observable Behavior and As-If Rule

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ObservableEffect
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: abstract-machine.observable-behavior
applies-to: optimizer, backend, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the observable-effect variants used by the abstract machine.
-->

ObservableEffect ∈ {
  HostEffect(proc, args),
  FfiEffect(proc, abi, dir),
  PanicEffect(kind),
  DropEffect(target),
  KeyEffect(kind, paths)
}

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ObservableEvent
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: abstract-machine.observable-behavior
applies-to: optimizer, backend, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines which execution events are observable.
-->

An event is observable iff it is:
- a runtime host-primitive action from `HostPrimRuntime`;
- transfer across an FFI boundary;
- panic initiation, panic-to-abort escalation, or a caught-unwind boundary result;
- invocation of drop cleanup for a responsible value or static;
- key acquisition, key release, or ordered key-block commit.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ObservableBehavior
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: abstract-machine.observable-behavior
applies-to: optimizer, backend, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines observable execution behavior as an ordered observable-event trace plus final outcome.
-->

The observable behavior of an execution is the ordered trace of its observable events together with its final outcome in `{normal, panic, abort}`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AsIfObservablePreservation
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: abstract-machine.observable-behavior
applies-to: optimizer, backend, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Allows only transformations whose executions preserve observable traces, cleanup order, host and FFI effect order, outcomes, key behavior, and permission/provenance/responsibility facts.
-->

A conforming implementation MAY apply any transformation whose executions preserve all of the following:
- the same observable-event trace at every sequence point;
- the same relative order of drop actions required by `CleanupScope`, `Unwind`, and `Destroy`;
- the same relative order of capability-mediated host effects and FFI-boundary effects induced by the source semantics;
- the same panic, non-panic, and abort outcomes, including the same `#unwind` boundary behavior;
- the same key-acquisition, key-release, and ordered-commit behavior required by Chapter `19`;
- the same permission, provenance, and responsibility facts required by Chapters `6`, `10`, `18`, `23`, and `24`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AsIfForbiddenObservableChanges
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: abstract-machine.observable-behavior
applies-to: optimizer, backend, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Forbids transformations that eliminate, duplicate, reorder, suppress, invent, or reverse required observable behavior.
-->

In particular, a conforming implementation MUST NOT:
- eliminate, duplicate, or reorder observable events;
- suppress or invent any `Drop` action required by the cleanup rules;
- reorder host effects or FFI-boundary effects across sequence points;
- transform a panicking execution into a non-panicking execution, or the reverse;
- introduce behavior that violates the key system, provenance rules, or no-ambient-authority rules.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 6.1.5 Sequence Points

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.SequencePoint
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: abstract-machine.sequence-points
applies-to: evaluator, optimizer, backend, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines sequence points in terms of completed prior observable effects, unstarted later observable effects, and determined machine state.
-->

A sequence point is a program point at which:
- all observable effects sequenced before that point are complete;
- no observable effect sequenced after that point has begun; and
- binding-state, provenance, and key-holding state are determined by the rules of the owning chapters.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.CanonicalSequencePoints
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: abstract-machine.sequence-points
applies-to: evaluator, optimizer, backend, runtime, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines canonical sequence-point locations in Ultraviolet execution.
-->

The canonical sequence points are:
- after each terminated statement;
- after receiver and argument evaluation and before control enters the callee of a call or method call;
- after the left operand of `&&` and `||` and before any right-operand evaluation that follows;
- after the condition of `if` and before the selected branch;
- after the scrutinee of `if ... is` and before pattern selection or selected-body evaluation;
- after key-path evaluation and before a key block acquires or commits keys;
- immediately before scope cleanup begins on ordinary scope exit, `return`, `break`, `continue`, panic unwinding, and FFI-boundary unwinding.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.SequencePointLTRPreservation
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: abstract-machine.sequence-points
applies-to: evaluator, optimizer, backend, runtime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires preservation of left-to-right subexpression order between adjacent sequence points unless observable behavior and sequence-point boundaries are preserved.
-->

`Children_LTR` in §24.7.7 defines left-to-right subexpression order inside a segment between adjacent sequence points. A conforming implementation MUST preserve that order unless an equivalent transformation preserves the same observable behavior and the same sequence-point boundaries.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 6.1.6 Unsafe and Foreign Interaction

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.UnsafeForeignAuthority
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: authority.unsafe-ffi
applies-to: type-checker, runtime, ffi, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: States that unsafe operations and FFI may escape no-ambient-authority constraints by design while capability isolation still applies.
-->

The no-ambient-authority requirements constrain the safe execution model. `unsafe` operations and the foreign-function interface MAY escape these constraints by design, but capability isolation still applies. See §23.5.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

### 6.2 Host Primitives

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.IOHostPrimitiveSets
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.host-primitives
applies-to: runtime, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines IO, file, and directory host primitive sets.
-->

IOPrim = {IOOpenRead, IOOpenWrite, IOOpenAppend, IOCreateWrite, IOReadFile, IOReadBytes, IOWriteFile, IOWriteStdout, IOWriteStderr, IOExists, IORemove, IOOpenDir, IOCreateDir, IOEnsureDir, IOKind, IORestrict}
FilePrim = {FileReadAll, FileReadAllBytes, FileWrite, FileFlush, FileClose}
DirPrim = {DirNext, DirClose}

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.OtherHostPrimitiveSets
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.host-primitives
applies-to: runtime, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines system, network, heap, reactor, time, and cancellation host primitive sets.
-->

SystemPrim = {SystemGetEnv, SystemExit, SystemRun}
NetworkPrim = {NetRestrictHost}
HeapPrim = {HeapWithQuota, HeapAllocRaw, HeapDeallocRaw}

Entries(⟨entries, handles, diriters, flushed, failmap⟩) = entries
Handles(⟨entries, handles, diriters, flushed, failmap⟩) = handles
DirIters(⟨entries, handles, diriters, flushed, failmap⟩) = diriters
FlushedSet(⟨entries, handles, diriters, flushed, failmap⟩) = flushed

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines filesystem entry kind and content queries.
-->

EntryKind(ω, path) =
 `File`  if Entries(ω)[path] = FileEntry(_)
 `Dir`   if Entries(ω)[path] = DirEntry(_)
 `Other` if Entries(ω)[path] = OtherEntry
 `Other` otherwise
FileBytes(ω, path) = bytes ⇔ Entries(ω)[path] = FileEntry(bytes)
DirNames(ω, path) = names ⇔ Entries(ω)[path] = DirEntry(names)

HandleStateOf(ω, h) =
 Handles(ω)[h].state  if Handles(ω)[h] defined
 `Closed`             otherwise
HandlePos(ω, h) =
 Handles(ω)[h].pos  if Handles(ω)[h] defined
 0                  otherwise
HandleLen(ω, h) =
 Handles(ω)[h].len  if Handles(ω)[h] defined
 0                  otherwise
HandlePath(ω, h) =
 Handles(ω)[h].path  if Handles(ω)[h] defined
 "\""                otherwise

DirIterPath(ω, h) =
 DirIters(ω)[h].path  if DirIters(ω)[h] defined
 "\""                 otherwise
DirIterEntries(ω, h) =
 DirIters(ω)[h].entries  if DirIters(ω)[h] defined
 []                      otherwise
DirIterPos(ω, h) =
 DirIters(ω)[h].pos  if DirIters(ω)[h] defined
 0                    otherwise
DirIterOpen(ω, h) ⇔ DirIters(ω)[h] defined

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.RestrictPathSuccess
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, path-resolution, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines successful restricted filesystem path resolution under a canonical base prefix.
-->

RestrictPath(base, path) = p ⇔ ¬ AbsPath(path) ∧ b = Canon(Normalize(base)) ∧ b ≠ ⊥ ∧ p = Canon(Normalize(Join(b, path))) ∧ p ≠ ⊥ ∧ prefix(p, b)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.RestrictPathFailure
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, path-resolution, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines failed restricted filesystem path resolution.
-->

RestrictPath(base, path) = ⊥ ⇔ AbsPath(path) ∨ Canon(Normalize(base)) = ⊥ ∨ Canon(Normalize(Join(Canon(Normalize(base)), path))) = ⊥ ∨ ¬ prefix(Canon(Normalize(Join(Canon(Normalize(base)), path))), Canon(Normalize(base)))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IORestrict-Delegate
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, path-resolution, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Restricted IO operations delegate to the parent filesystem at the restricted resolved path.
labels: IORestrict-Delegate
-->

IORestrict(io, base) ⇓ io' ∧ Op ∈ IOOp ∧ RestrictPath(base, p) = q ⇒ Op(io', p) = Op(io, q)

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IORestrict-InvalidPath
kind: formal-rule

applies-to: runtime, capabilities, path-resolution, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Restricted IO operations other than exists return invalid-path errors when path restriction fails.
labels: IORestrict-InvalidPath
-->

IORestrict(io, base) ⇓ io' ∧ Op ∈ IOOp ∧ RestrictPath(base, p) = ⊥ ∧ Op ≠ IOExists ⇒ Op(io', p) = IoError::InvalidPath

kind: formal-rule

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

Busy(io, path, Op, ω) ⇔ FailMap(ω)[⟨Op, path⟩] = IoError::Busy

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.IORemoveSemantics
kind: formal-definition

strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines non-recursive IO remove helper relations and state update helpers.

NonEmptyDir(ω, path) ⇔ Entries(ω)[path] = DirEntry(names) ∧ ∃ name ∈ names. name ≠ "." ∧ name ≠ ".."
ParentPath(path) =

 JoinComp([ PathComps(path)[i] | 0 ≤ i < |PathComps(path)| - 1 ])  otherwise

 DirEntry(RemoveName(names, Basename(path)))  if q = ParentPath(path) ∧ Entries(ω)[q] = DirEntry(names)
 Entries(ω)[q]                                otherwise
IORemoveEntries(ω, path) = { q ↦ RemoveEntryAt(ω, path, q) | q ∈ dom(Entries(ω)) ∧ q ≠ path }
IORemoveClear(io, path, ω) ⇔ ¬ PathInvalid(io, path, ω) ∧ EntryExists(ω, path) ∧ ¬ PermissionDenied(io, path, IORemove, ω) ∧ ¬ Busy(io, path, IORemove, ω) ∧ ¬ OtherFailure(io, path, IORemove, ω)

`IORemove` is not recursive. A successful `IORemove` removes exactly the named
entry and the corresponding name from its parent directory entry. It does not
remove descendant entries, and it does not follow `OtherEntry` entries such as
symbolic links.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IORemove-RemoveFile
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, filesystem, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO remove succeeds for file entries by removing exactly the named entry.
labels: IORemove-RemoveFile
-->

IORemoveClear(io, path, ω) ∧ Entries(ω)[path] = FileEntry(_) ∧ IORemove(io, path, ω) ⇓ ((), ω') ⇒ Entries(ω') = IORemoveEntries(ω, path) ∧ Handles(ω') = Handles(ω) ∧ DirIters(ω') = DirIters(ω) ∧ FlushedSet(ω') = FlushedSet(ω) ∧ FailMap(ω') = FailMap(ω)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IORemove-RemoveOtherEntry
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, filesystem, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO remove succeeds for other filesystem entries by removing the entry itself without following it.
labels: IORemove-RemoveOtherEntry
-->

IORemoveClear(io, path, ω) ∧ Entries(ω)[path] = OtherEntry ∧ IORemove(io, path, ω) ⇓ ((), ω') ⇒ Entries(ω') = IORemoveEntries(ω, path) ∧ Handles(ω') = Handles(ω) ∧ DirIters(ω') = DirIters(ω) ∧ FlushedSet(ω') = FlushedSet(ω) ∧ FailMap(ω') = FailMap(ω)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IORemove-RemoveEmptyDir
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, filesystem, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO remove succeeds for empty directories by removing exactly the named directory entry.
labels: IORemove-RemoveEmptyDir
-->

IORemoveClear(io, path, ω) ∧ Entries(ω)[path] = DirEntry(_) ∧ ¬ NonEmptyDir(ω, path) ∧ IORemove(io, path, ω) ⇓ ((), ω') ⇒ Entries(ω') = IORemoveEntries(ω, path) ∧ Handles(ω') = Handles(ω) ∧ DirIters(ω') = DirIters(ω) ∧ FlushedSet(ω') = FlushedSet(ω) ∧ FailMap(ω') = FailMap(ω)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IORemove-DirectoryNotEmpty
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, diagnostics, filesystem, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO remove returns DirectoryNotEmpty when the named directory has child entries.
labels: IORemove-DirectoryNotEmpty
-->

IORemoveClear(io, path, ω) ∧ NonEmptyDir(ω, path) ⇒ IORemove(io, path, ω) ⇓ (IoError::DirectoryNotEmpty, ω)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOReadFile-InvalidUtf8
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO text reads return IoFailure when the corresponding byte read is not valid UTF-8.
labels: IOReadFile-InvalidUtf8
-->

IOReadFile(io, path, ω) ⇓ (r, ω') ∧ IOReadBytes(io, path, ω) ⇓ (bytes, ω'') ∧ ¬ Utf8Valid(bytes) ⇒ r = IoError::IoFailure

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileReadAll-InvalidUtf8
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: File text reads return IoFailure when the corresponding byte read is not valid UTF-8.
labels: FileReadAll-InvalidUtf8
-->

FileReadAll(h, ω) ⇓ (r, ω') ∧ FileReadAllBytes(h, ω) ⇓ (bytes, ω'') ∧ ¬ Utf8Valid(bytes) ⇒ r = IoError::IoFailure

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOExists-True
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO existence true results imply an existing, valid path.
labels: IOExists-True
-->

IOExists(io, path, ω) ⇓ (true, ω') ⇒ EntryExists(ω, path) ∧ ¬ PathInvalid(io, path, ω)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOExists-False
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO existence false results imply an invalid path or missing entry.
labels: IOExists-False
-->

IOExists(io, path, ω) ⇓ (false, ω') ⇒ PathInvalid(io, path, ω) ∨ ¬ EntryExists(ω, path)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.FileHandleStateAndMode
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines file handle states, open-handle predicate, and handle mode projection.
-->

HandleState = {`OpenRead`, `OpenWrite`, `OpenAppend`, `Closed`}
HandleOpen(ω, h) ⇔ HandleStateOf(ω, h) ≠ `Closed`
HandleMode(ω, h) =
 `Read`    if HandleStateOf(ω, h) = `OpenRead`
 `Write`   if HandleStateOf(ω, h) = `OpenWrite`
 `Append`  if HandleStateOf(ω, h) = `OpenAppend`

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.FileLengthAndByteLength
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines file length at path and byte length for byte and string data.
-->

FileLenAt(ω, path) =
 ByteLen(bytes)  if Entries(ω)[path] = FileEntry(bytes)
 0               otherwise
ByteLen(data) =
 |data|       if data ∈ Bytes
 |Utf8(data)| if data ∈ String
 0            otherwise

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.DirectoryEntryOrdering
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines byte lexicographic ordering, directory entry keys, directory snapshots, and ordered directory entries.
-->

LexBytes(b_1, b_2) ⇔ (∃ k. 0 ≤ k < min(|b_1|, |b_2|) ∧ (∀ i < k. b_1[i] = b_2[i]) ∧ b_1[k] < b_2[k]) ∨ (|b_1| < |b_2| ∧ ∀ i < |b_1|. b_1[i] = b_2[i])
EntryKey(name) = CaseFold(NFC(name))
EntryOrder(a, b) ⇔ LexBytes(Utf8(EntryKey(a)), Utf8(EntryKey(b))) ∨ (EntryKey(a) = EntryKey(b) ∧ LexBytes(Utf8(a), Utf8(b)))
DirSnapshot(io, path, ω) =
 [ `DirEntry`{`path`: Join(path, name), `name`: name, `kind`: EntryKind(ω, Join(path, name))} | name ∈ DirNames(ω, path) ∧ name ≠ "." ∧ name ≠ ".." ]  if Entries(ω)[path] = DirEntry(_)
 []                                                                                                                        otherwise
DirEntries(io, path, ω) = sort_{λ a, b. EntryOrder(a.name, b.name)}(DirSnapshot(io, path, ω))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOOpenRead-HandleState
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful read-open creates an open-read handle at position zero with source path and length.
labels: IOOpenRead-HandleState
-->

IOOpenRead(io, path, ω) ⇓ (`File@Read`{`handle`: h}, ω') ⇒ HandleStateOf(ω', h) = `OpenRead` ∧ HandlePos(ω', h) = 0 ∧ HandlePath(ω', h) = path ∧ HandleLen(ω', h) = FileLenAt(ω, path)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOOpenWrite-HandleState
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful write-open creates an open-write handle at position zero with source path and length.
labels: IOOpenWrite-HandleState
-->

IOOpenWrite(io, path, ω) ⇓ (`File@Write`{`handle`: h}, ω') ⇒ HandleStateOf(ω', h) = `OpenWrite` ∧ HandlePos(ω', h) = 0 ∧ HandlePath(ω', h) = path ∧ HandleLen(ω', h) = FileLenAt(ω, path)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOOpenAppend-HandleState
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful append-open creates an open-append handle positioned at file end with source path and length.
labels: IOOpenAppend-HandleState
-->

IOOpenAppend(io, path, ω) ⇓ (`File@Append`{`handle`: h}, ω') ⇒ HandleStateOf(ω', h) = `OpenAppend` ∧ HandlePos(ω', h) = FileLenAt(ω, path) ∧ HandlePath(ω', h) = path ∧ HandleLen(ω', h) = FileLenAt(ω, path)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOCreateWrite-HandleState
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful create-write creates an open-write handle at position zero with zero length.
labels: IOCreateWrite-HandleState
-->

IOCreateWrite(io, path, ω) ⇓ (`File@Write`{`handle`: h}, ω') ⇒ HandleStateOf(ω', h) = `OpenWrite` ∧ HandlePos(ω', h) = 0 ∧ HandlePath(ω', h) = path ∧ HandleLen(ω', h) = 0

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOReadFile-DelegatesThroughHandle
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO text file reads open, read all, and close a read handle.
labels: IOReadFile-DelegatesThroughHandle
-->

IOReadFile(io, path, ω) ⇓ (r, ω') ⇔ ∃ h, ω_1, ω_2. IOOpenRead(io, path, ω) ⇓ (`File@Read`{`handle`: h}, ω_1) ∧ FileReadAll(h, ω_1) ⇓ (r, ω_2) ∧ FileClose(h, ω_2) ⇓ (ok, ω')

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOReadBytes-DelegatesThroughHandle
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: IO byte file reads open, read all bytes, and close a read handle.
labels: IOReadBytes-DelegatesThroughHandle
-->

IOReadBytes(io, path, ω) ⇓ (r, ω') ⇔ ∃ h, ω_1, ω_2. IOOpenRead(io, path, ω) ⇓ (`File@Read`{`handle`: h}, ω_1) ∧ FileReadAllBytes(h, ω_1) ⇓ (r, ω_2) ∧ FileClose(h, ω_2) ⇓ (ok, ω')

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileReadAll-ClosedFailure
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Reading text from a closed file handle fails with IoFailure.
labels: FileReadAll-ClosedFailure
-->

¬ HandleOpen(ω, h) ⇒ FileReadAll(h, ω) ⇓ (IoError::IoFailure, ω)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileReadAllBytes-ClosedFailure
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileWrite-ClosedFailure
kind: formal-rule

kind: formal-rule

-->

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileReadAll-AdvancesToEnd
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful text reads advance the handle position to the handle length.
labels: FileReadAll-AdvancesToEnd
-->

FileReadAll(h, ω) ⇓ (r, ω') ∧ r ≠ IoError::IoFailure ⇒ HandlePos(ω', h) = HandleLen(ω, h)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileReadAllBytes-AdvancesToEnd
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful byte reads advance the handle position to the handle length.
labels: FileReadAllBytes-AdvancesToEnd
-->

FileReadAllBytes(h, ω) ⇓ (r, ω') ∧ r ≠ IoError::IoFailure ⇒ HandlePos(ω', h) = HandleLen(ω, h)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileWrite-PositionUpdate
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful file writes require an open handle and update position by append or current-position mode.
labels: FileWrite-PositionUpdate
-->

FileWrite(h, data, ω) ⇓ (ok, ω') ⇒ HandleOpen(ω, h) ∧ (HandleMode(ω, h) = `Append` ⇒ HandlePos(ω', h) = HandleLen(ω, h) + ByteLen(data)) ∧ (HandleMode(ω, h) ≠ `Append` ⇒ HandlePos(ω', h) = HandlePos(ω, h) + ByteLen(data))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileWrite-LengthUpdate
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful file writes update handle length to the max of previous length and new position.
labels: FileWrite-LengthUpdate
-->

FileWrite(h, data, ω) ⇓ (ok, ω') ⇒ HandleLen(ω', h) = max(HandleLen(ω, h), HandlePos(ω', h))

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

id: FileFlush-RecordsFlushed
kind: formal-rule

applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: FileClose-ClosesHandle
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: IOOpenDir-IteratorState
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful directory open creates an open iterator over ordered directory entries at position zero.
labels: IOOpenDir-IteratorState
-->

IOOpenDir(io, path, ω) ⇓ (`DirIter@Open`{`handle`: h}, ω') ⇒ DirIterOpen(ω', h) ∧ DirIterIO(ω', h) = io ∧ DirIterPath(ω', h) = path ∧ DirIterEntries(ω', h) = DirEntries(io, path, ω) ∧ DirIterPos(ω', h) = 0

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: DirNext-ClosedFailure
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Directory next on a closed iterator fails with IoFailure.
labels: DirNext-ClosedFailure
-->

¬ DirIterOpen(ω, h) ⇒ DirNext(h, ω) ⇓ (IoError::IoFailure, ω)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: DirNext-Exhausted
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Directory next returns unit when an open iterator is exhausted.
labels: DirNext-Exhausted
-->

DirIterOpen(ω, h) ∧ DirIterPos(ω, h) = i ∧ i ≥ |DirIterEntries(ω, h)| ⇒ DirNext(h, ω) ⇓ ((), ω)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: DirNext-YieldsEntry
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Directory next returns the current entry and advances iterator position.
labels: DirNext-YieldsEntry
-->

DirIterOpen(ω, h) ∧ DirIterPos(ω, h) = i ∧ i < |DirIterEntries(ω, h)| ∧ entry = DirIterEntries(ω, h)[i] ⇒ DirNext(h, ω) ⇓ (entry, ω_2) ∧ DirIterPos(ω_2, h) = i + 1

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: DirClose-ClosesIterator
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.io-primitives
applies-to: runtime, capabilities, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Successful directory close marks the iterator no longer open.

-->

DirClose(h, ω) ⇓ (ok, ω') ⇒ ¬ DirIterOpen(ω', h)
