### 8.4 Metatheoretic Properties

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: property.TypeSystemMetatheory.Intro
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Introduces the key metatheoretic properties that the Ultraviolet type system is designed to satisfy.
-->

This subsection states the key metatheoretic properties that the Ultraviolet type system is designed to satisfy. Formal proofs are deferred to supplementary materials.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Progress
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Progress from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: Progress
-->

**(Progress)**
If Γ ⊢ e : T and `e` is not a value, then either:
1. `e` can take a step.
2. `e` is blocked on an external operation.
3. `e` panics.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Preservation
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Preservation from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: Preservation
-->

**(Preservation)**
If Γ ⊢ e : T and `e → e'`, then Γ ⊢ e' : T.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: No-Use-After-Free
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines No-Use-After-Free from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: No-Use-After-Free
-->

**(No-Use-After-Free)**
A binding in state `Moved` or `PartiallyMoved(F)` where `f ∈ F` cannot be read or moved from.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: No-Double-Free
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines No-Double-Free from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: No-Double-Free
-->

**(No-Double-Free)**
Each responsible binding is dropped exactly once when it goes out of scope.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: No-Dangling-Pointers
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines No-Dangling-Pointers from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: No-Dangling-Pointers
-->

**(No-Dangling-Pointers)**
A pointer `Ptr<T>@Valid` always references valid storage. A pointer with provenance `π` cannot escape to storage with longer lifetime `π'` where `π < π'`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Exclusivity-Invariant
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Exclusivity-Invariant from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: Exclusivity-Invariant
-->

**(Exclusivity-Invariant)**
If a binding `x` has permission `unique` and is in state `Active`, then no other live path exists to the same storage location.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Permission-Preservation
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Permission-Preservation from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: Permission-Preservation
-->

**(Permission-Preservation)**
Permissions are preserved as permission regimes. Admissibility at a use site MUST NOT create a weaker alias or convert a `unique` binding into `shared` or `const`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: State-Determinism
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines State-Determinism from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: State-Determinism
-->

**(State-Determinism)**
At each program point, every binding has exactly one state in `{Valid, Moved, PartiallyMoved(F)}`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: No-Resurrection
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines No-Resurrection from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: No-Resurrection
-->

**(No-Resurrection)**
A binding in state `Moved` cannot transition back to `Valid` except through reassignment of a `var` binding.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Data-Race-Freedom
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Data-Race-Freedom from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: Data-Race-Freedom
-->

**(Data-Race-Freedom)**
Concurrent accesses to `shared` data are serialized through the key system.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Fork-Join-Guarantee
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Fork-Join-Guarantee from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: Fork-Join-Guarantee
-->

**(Fork-Join-Guarantee)**
All work items spawned within a `parallel` block complete before the block exits.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Key-Serialization
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Key-Serialization from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: Key-Serialization
-->

**(Key-Serialization)**
If two tasks hold keys `K₁` and `K₂` to overlapping paths with incompatible modes, the key system ensures they do not execute concurrently.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Async-Key-Safety
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, runtime, ownership, permissions, async, parallelism, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Async-Key-Safety from properties.TypeSystemMetatheory.
labels: Async-Key-Safety
-->

**(Async-Key-Safety)**
Keys cannot be held across `yield` or `wait` suspension points unless the `release` modifier is used.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->


### 8.5 Core Type Diagnostics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: diagnostics.CoreTypeDiagnostics
kind: diagnostics
phase: diagnostics
strength: required
owner: diagnostics.types
applies-to: semantic-analysis, type-system, generics, inference, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines core type-inference, alias-cycle, variance, and literal suffix diagnostic code table.
-->

This section owns core type-inference and alias-cycle diagnostics that are not specific to a single feature chapter.

| Code         | Severity | Detection    | Condition                                                  |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `E-TYP-1506` | Error    | Compile-time | Type alias cycle detected                                  |
| `E-TYP-1520` | Error    | Compile-time | Invariant type parameter requires exact type match         |
| `E-TYP-1521` | Error    | Compile-time | Covariant or contravariant generic variance requirement not satisfied |
| `E-TYP-1530` | Error    | Compile-time | Type inference failed; unable to determine type            |
| `E-TYP-1531` | Error    | Compile-time | Float literal explicit suffix does not match expected type |

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

## 9. Attributes and Metadata

### 9.1 Attribute Syntax and Placement

#### 9.1.1 Syntax

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.AttributeSyntaxAndPlacement
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.attributes
applies-to: parsing, attributes, oracle.syntax, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines attribute list grammar, attribute names, vendor prefixes, and attribute arguments.
-->

```ebnf
attribute_list    ::= attribute+
attribute         ::= "#" attribute_spec
attribute_spec    ::= attribute_name ("(" attribute_args? ")")?
attribute_name    ::= identifier
                    | "dynamic"
                    | "static"
                    | vendor_prefix "::" identifier
                    | vendor_prefix "::" "dynamic"
                    | vendor_prefix "::" "static"
vendor_prefix     ::= identifier ("::" identifier)*
attribute_args    ::= attribute_arg ("," attribute_arg)* ","?
attribute_arg     ::= literal
                    | identifier
                    | identifier ":" literal
                    | identifier ":" identifier
                    | identifier "(" attribute_args? ")"
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AttributeReservedLeafNames
kind: normative-requirement
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.attributes
applies-to: parsing, attributes, vendor-attributes, diagnostics, oracle.syntax, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires dynamic and static to appear only as attribute-name leaves and not inside vendor prefixes.
-->

The reserved names `dynamic` and `static` are admitted only in the leaf position of `attribute_name`. They MUST NOT appear inside `vendor_prefix`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.AttributeImmediateTargetPlacement
kind: normative-requirement
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.attributes
applies-to: parsing, attributes, diagnostics, oracle.syntax, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires an attribute list to appear immediately before the declaration or expression it modifies.
-->

An attribute list MUST appear immediately before the declaration or expression it modifies.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.attributes
applies-to: parsing, ast, attributes, vendor-attributes, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines vendor attribute AST form as scoped attribute names with identifier or dynamic/static leaves and identifier-only prefix segments.
-->

Vendor-defined attribute names use the scoped `AttrName` form `⟨vendor_prefix, leaf⟩`, where `leaf` is an `identifier` or one of the reserved verification-mode names `dynamic` or `static`. `vendor_prefix` segments are always `identifier` tokens.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.2.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.VendorAttributeStaticSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, vendor-attributes, reserved-names, diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires vendor attributes to use scoped prefixes, reserves the ultraviolet namespace, and fixes R_vendor as empty so non-spec attributes are rejected.
-->

Vendor-defined attributes in `R_vendor` MUST use scoped prefixes of the form `vendor::name` or `com::vendor::name`.

The `ultraviolet::...` namespace is reserved for specification-defined attributes.

`R_vendor = ∅`. Any attribute name not in `R_spec` is rejected as unknown.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

### 9.3 Layout Attributes

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.LayoutAttributeSyntax
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.attributes.layout
applies-to: parsing, attributes, layout, oracle.syntax, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines layout attribute syntax, layout arguments, layout kinds, and integer layout types.
-->

#### 9.3.1 Syntax

```ebnf
layout_attribute ::= attr_open "layout" "(" layout_args ")" attr_close
layout_args      ::= layout_kind ("," layout_kind)*
layout_kind      ::= "C" | "packed" | "align" "(" integer_literal ")" | int_type
int_type         ::= "i8" | "i16" | "i32" | "i64" | "u8" | "u16" | "u32" | "u64"
``` 

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.3.2 Parsing

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

Layout attributes are parsed by the general attribute parser in §9.1.2. This section introduces no additional parsing rules.

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

owner: parser.attributes.layout
applies-to: parsing, ast, attributes, layout, records, enums, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines layout attributes as ordinary attribute specs attached to record or enum declarations.
-->

Layout attributes are ordinary `AttributeSpec` entries attached to `RecordDecl` or `EnumDecl`.

#### 9.3.4 Static Semantics

**`#layout(C)`.** Specifies C-compatible memory layout.

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.LayoutCRecordSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, records, abi, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires layout(C) records to use declaration order, C ABI padding only, and size aligned to record alignment.
-->

For `record` declarations:
1. Fields MUST be laid out in declaration order.
2. Padding MUST be inserted only as required by the target platform's C ABI.
3. Total size MUST be a multiple of the record's alignment.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.LayoutCEnumSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, enums, abi, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires layout(C) enums to use C-compatible integer tags, DiscType defaults, and tagged-union C ABI layout.
-->

For `enum` declarations:
1. The discriminant MUST be represented as a C-compatible integer tag.
2. Default tag type is `DiscType(E)` as defined by §12.7.
3. Layout MUST conform to a tagged union per the target C ABI.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.LayoutExplicitEnumDiscriminant
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, enums, abi, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires explicit enum discriminant layout to use the specified integer type, represent all variant values, and apply only to enums.
-->

**`#layout(IntType)` (explicit discriminant).** For an `enum` marked `#layout(IntType)` where `IntType` is `i8`–`i64` or `u8`–`u64`:
1. The discriminant MUST use the specified integer type.
2. Each variant's discriminant value MUST be representable in that type.
3. This form is valid only on `enum` declarations.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

**`#layout(packed)`.** Removes inter-field padding.

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.LayoutPackedRecordSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, records, abi, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires packed records to remove inter-field padding and use alignment 1 for fields and the record.
-->

For a `record` marked `#layout(packed)`:
1. All inter-field padding is removed.
2. Each field MUST be laid out with alignment 1.
3. The record's overall alignment becomes 1.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.PackedFieldReferenceRequiresUnsafe
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, records, unsafe, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires references to packed fields to occur only inside unsafe blocks.
-->

Taking a reference to a packed field MUST occur within an `unsafe` block. Outside `unsafe`, the program is ill-formed.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

**`#layout(align(N))`.** Sets a minimum alignment.

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.LayoutAlignSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, abi, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires align(N) to use positive power-of-two N, compute effective alignment, and pad size to that alignment.
-->

1. N MUST be a positive integer that is a power of two.
2. Effective alignment is max(N, natural alignment).
3. If N < natural alignment, natural alignment is used.
4. Type size is padded to a multiple of the effective alignment.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

**Compile-time layout verification**

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ValidLayoutAttributeCombinations
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines valid layout attribute argument combinations.
-->

Valid combinations:
- `layout(C)`
- `layout(packed)`
- `layout(align(N))`
- `layout(C, packed)`
- `layout(C, align(N))`
- `layout(u8)`

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-definition

owner: checker.attributes.layout

-->

Invalid combinations:
- `layout(packed, align(N))`

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.LayoutAttributeApplicability
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, records, enums, modal-types, generics, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines declaration-kind applicability for layout arguments.
-->

Applicability constraints:
- `record`: `C`, `packed`, `align(N)`
- `enum`: `C`, `align(N)`, `IntType`
- `modal`: none
- generic (unmonomorphized): none

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.LayoutAttributeConstraints
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.layout
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, layout, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires invalid packed targets, non-power-of-two alignments, conflicting layout arguments, and low alignments to produce the specified errors or warnings.
-->

Constraints:
1. `layout(packed)` applied to a non-`record` declaration is ill-formed.
2. `layout(align(N))` where N is not a power of two is ill-formed.
3. Conflicting layout arguments, including `layout(packed, align(N))`, are ill-formed.
4. `layout(align(N))` where N < natural alignment emits a warning.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.3.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.attributes.layout
applies-to: runtime, attributes, layout, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires layout attributes to introduce no direct runtime mechanism and packed-field reference safety to be statically enforced.

Layout attributes introduce no direct runtime mechanism. Packed-field reference safety is enforced statically at the use site.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.3.6 Lowering

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.LayoutAttributeLowering
kind: lowering-rule
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: lowering.attributes.layout
applies-to: lowering, attributes, layout, abi, oracle.coverage

-->

Layout attributes constrain the layout and ABI calculations used by Chapter 24. `layout(C)` selects target C-ABI layout, `layout(packed)` removes inter-field padding and lowers effective alignment to 1, `layout(align(N))` raises minimum alignment, and `layout(IntType)` selects the enum discriminant representation.

### 9.4 Optimization Attributes

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.OptimizationAttributeSyntax
kind: grammar

applies-to: parsing, attributes, optimization, oracle.syntax, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines inline and cold optimization attribute syntax.
-->

#### 9.4.1 Syntax

```ebnf
inline_attribute ::= attr_open "inline" ("(" inline_mode ")")? attr_close
inline_mode      ::= "always" | "never" | "default"

cold_attribute   ::= attr_open "cold" attr_close
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.4.2 Parsing

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: semantic-requirement

applies-to: parsing, attributes, optimization, oracle.syntax, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires optimization attributes to use the general attribute parser and introduce no additional parsing rules.
-->

Optimization attributes are parsed by the general attribute parser in §9.1.2. This section introduces no additional parsing rules.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.4.3 AST Representation / Form

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.OptimizationAttributeAstAttachment
kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.attributes.optimization
applies-to: parsing, ast, attributes, optimization, procedures, methods, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines optimization attributes as ordinary attribute specs attached to procedure or method declarations.
-->

Optimization attributes are ordinary `AttributeSpec` entries attached to `ProcedureDecl` or `MethodDecl`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.4.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.InlineAttributeSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.optimization
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, optimization, lowering, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines inline, inline(always), inline(default), and inline(never) optimization semantics.
-->

**`#inline`.** The implementation SHOULD inline the procedure at call sites when feasible.

**`#inline(always)`.** The implementation SHOULD inline the procedure at all call sites. If inlining is not possible, such as for recursive procedures or procedures whose address is taken, the implementation SHOULD emit a warning.

**`#inline(default)`.** Equivalent to omitting the attribute.

**`#inline(never)`.** The implementation MUST NOT inline the procedure. The procedure body MUST be emitted as a separate callable unit.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.ColdAttributeSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.optimization
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, optimization, lowering, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines cold as an optimization hint for procedures unlikely to execute during typical runs.
-->

**`#cold`.** Marks a procedure as unlikely to execute during typical runs. The implementation MAY use this as an optimization hint.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.4.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.attributes.optimization
applies-to: runtime, attributes, optimization, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires optimization attributes not to change language-level runtime semantics.
-->

Optimization attributes do not change the language-level runtime semantics of the annotated procedure.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.4.6 Lowering

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.OptimizationAttributeLowering
kind: lowering-rule
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: lowering.attributes.optimization
applies-to: lowering, attributes, optimization, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines optimization attribute lowering effects for inlining and cold code layout.
-->

`#inline(always)` and `#inline(never)` constrain procedure inlining decisions during lowering. `#inline(never)` requires emission of a separate callable unit. `#cold` MAY influence code layout or backend optimization heuristics.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.DynamicScopeDetermination
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.metadata
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, dynamic-verification, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires dynamic scope to be lexical and determined by dynamic declarations or attributed expressions.
-->

Scope determination:
1. `e` is within a `#dynamic` scope if it is enclosed by a `#dynamic` declaration, or by an attributed expression.
2. Scope is lexical and does not propagate through procedure calls.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ComputeDynamicContext
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.metadata
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, dynamic-verification, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines dynamic-context computation from a span and ancestor list.
-->

ComputeDynamicContext : Span × AncestorList → Bool

```text
ComputeDynamicContext(s, ancestors) =
  let enclosing_dynamic = FindInnermostDynamic(s, ancestors)
  match enclosing_dynamic {
    ⊥            → false
    Some(_)      → true
  }
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.FindInnermostDynamic
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.metadata
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, dynamic-verification, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines innermost dynamic ancestor lookup for a span and ancestor list.
-->

FindInnermostDynamic : Span × AncestorList → Option<Span>

```text
FindInnermostDynamic(s, ancestors) =
  let dynamic_ancestors = [a | a ∈ ancestors ∧ (DynamicDecl(a) ∨ DynamicExpr(a)) ∧ s ⊆ a.span]
  if dynamic_ancestors = [] then ⊥
  else Some(MinimalSpan(dynamic_ancestors))
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.MinimalSpan
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.metadata
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, dynamic-verification, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines minimal-span selection from syntactic forms.
-->

MinimalSpan : [SyntacticForm] → Span

```text
MinimalSpan(forms) = argmin_{f ∈ forms} |f.span|
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

labels: DynamicContext-Override

**(DynamicContext-Override)**
```
ClassProc(C, m) has #dynamic    ClassImpl(T, C) has override m
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ComputeDynamicContext(override.body.span, Ancestors(override)) = true
```

summary: Requires reflectable declarations to expose canonical shape, member order, and attached attributes during Phase 2 reflection.
-->

**`#reflect`.** Marks a `record`, `enum`, or `modal` declaration as reflectable during Phase 2. Reflection queries over such declarations are defined by §22.3. A conforming implementation MUST expose the declaration's canonical shape, member order, and attached attributes to the compile-time reflection environment.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.DeriveAttributeSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.metadata
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, derive, comptime, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires derive attributes to schedule Phase 2 derive-target execution under Chapter 22 rules.
-->

**`#derive(... )`.** Schedules derive-target execution in Phase 2 for the annotated `record`, `enum`, or `modal` declaration. Derive target resolution, dependency ordering, and contract checking are defined by §22.5.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.EmitAttributeSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.metadata
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, comptime, generated-code, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires emit to grant TypeEmitter only to comptime statements or expressions, with ordering and visibility owned by Chapter 22.
-->

**`#emit`.** Grants the `TypeEmitter` capability to the annotated compile-time statement or compile-time expression. The target MUST be a `comptime` form. Emission ordering and generated-item visibility are defined by §22.4.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.FilesAttributeSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes.metadata
applies-to: semantic-analysis, attributes, comptime, project-files, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires files to grant ProjectFiles only to comptime statements or expressions, with snapshot and confinement semantics owned by Chapter 22.
-->

**`#files`.** Grants the `ProjectFiles` capability to the annotated compile-time statement or compile-time expression. The target MUST be a `comptime` form. File snapshot and path-confinement semantics are defined by §22.2.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.5.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.DiagnosticsMetadataDynamicSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.attributes.metadata
applies-to: runtime, attributes, dynamic-verification, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines runtime behavior for deprecated, stale_ok, static, and dynamic metadata attributes.
-->

`#deprecated`, `#stale_ok`, and `#static` introduce no direct runtime behavior in this chapter.

For `#dynamic`, runtime synchronization or runtime verification MUST be inserted exactly when required by the owning chapters for keys, contracts, refinements, and foreign contracts, and MUST NOT be inserted otherwise.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.5.6 Lowering

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.DiagnosticsMetadataLowering
kind: lowering-rule
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: lowering.attributes.metadata
applies-to: lowering, attributes, dynamic-verification, reflection, derive, comptime, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines lowering effects for dynamic, stale_ok, deprecated, reflect, derive, emit, and files attributes.
-->

`#dynamic` lowers by enabling runtime synchronization or runtime checks exactly where the owning semantic sections require them and nowhere else. `#stale_ok` suppresses warnings only and does not affect lowering. `#deprecated` introduces no lowering. `#reflect`, `#derive(... )`, `#emit`, and `#files` lower only through Phase 2 execution as defined by Chapter 22 and MUST introduce no direct Phase 4 runtime instrumentation.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

summary: Defines diagnostics for deprecated references, invalid dynamic targets, and empty dynamic scopes.
-->

| Code         | Severity | Detection    | Condition                                                                |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `W-CNF-0601` | Warning  | Compile-time | Reference to declaration marked `#deprecated`                         |
| `E-CON-0410` | Error    | Compile-time | `#dynamic` applied to contract clause directly                        |
| `E-CON-0411` | Error    | Compile-time | `#dynamic` applied to type alias declaration                          |
| `E-CON-0412` | Error    | Compile-time | `#dynamic` applied to field declaration                               |
| `W-CON-0401` | Warning  | Compile-time | `#dynamic` present but all proofs succeed statically                  |

### 9.6 Source-Native Test Attributes

#### 9.6.1 Syntax

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.TestAttribute
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.attributes
applies-to: parsing, attributes, testing, oracle.grammar, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the source-native test attribute grammar.
labels: test_attribute, test_attribute_args, test_attribute_arg
-->
```ebnf
test_attribute      ::= attr_open "test" ("(" test_attribute_args ")")? attr_close
test_attribute_args ::= test_attribute_arg ("," test_attribute_arg)*
test_attribute_arg  ::= "name" ":" string_literal
                      | "covers" "(" string_literal ")"
```
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.6.2 Parsing

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: parse.TestAttributeByOrdinaryAttributeParser
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.attributes
applies-to: parsing, attributes, testing, oracle.parser, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires test attributes to use the ordinary attribute parser representation.
-->

`#test` is parsed by the ordinary attribute parser from §9.1.2. The `name`
argument is represented as `⟨name, string_literal⟩`. Each `covers(...)` argument
is represented as `⟨covers, [string_literal]⟩`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.6.3 AST Representation / Form

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: ast.TestProcedureClassification
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes
applies-to: attributes, testing, procedures, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines source-native tests as ordinary procedure declarations carrying the test attribute.
-->

A source-native test is an ordinary `ProcedureDecl` whose `AttrByName(proc,
test)` set is non-empty.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TestName
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes
applies-to: attributes, testing, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines stable and display names for source-native tests.
-->

TestName(proc) = s when the unique `name: s` argument is present.
TestName(proc) = FullyQualifiedProcPath(proc) when no `name` argument is present.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TestCoverage
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes
applies-to: attributes, testing, conformance, obligation-ledger, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines coverage references carried by source-native tests.
-->

TestCoverage(proc) = [r_1, …, r_n] where each r_i is the string argument of one
`covers(r_i)` entry in source order.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.6.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.TestAttributeProcedureTarget
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes
applies-to: attributes, testing, procedures, diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires test attributes to apply only to ordinary source procedures.
-->

`#test` is valid only on ordinary source procedures.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TestAttributeArgsOk
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.attributes
applies-to: attributes, testing, conformance, obligation-ledger, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines well-formed argument rules for the test attribute.
-->

`AttrArgsOk(test, args)` holds exactly when:

1. every argument is either `name: string_literal` or `covers(string_literal)`;
2. at most one `name` argument is present;
3. every `covers` argument has exactly one non-empty string literal argument;
4. every coverage reference names one row in the obligation ledger using
   `obligation-id@Linternal_spec_line`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.TestProcedureShape
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.procedures
applies-to: attributes, testing, procedures, contracts, diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines required procedure shape for source-native tests.
-->

A `#test` procedure MUST:

1. have a body;
2. be non-generic;
3. have explicit visibility;
4. have an explicit return type;
5. have a contract clause containing a postcondition;
6. have either no parameters or exactly one parameter whose type is the
   toolchain-provided `TestAuthority` type.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.TestAuthority
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.procedures
applies-to: testing, authority, procedures, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines TestAuthority as the only runner-injected authority and time value for source-native tests.
-->

The `TestAuthority` parameter is the only runner-injected value. It carries the
filesystem, process, temporary-directory, target-profile, compiler-invocation,
and time authority needed by effectful compiler tests and benchmark-style tests.
Its `time` field has type `$Time`; tests that measure elapsed time SHOULD use
`time~>monotonic()`; `time~>wall()` is for UTC behavior, not benchmarks.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.6.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.TestAttributeDynamicSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: driver.tests
applies-to: testing, procedures, contracts, runtime, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines source-native test pass, fail, and error categories through ordinary procedure execution and postconditions.
-->

`#test` does not change ordinary procedure execution. During test execution,
the runner calls each discovered test procedure. A test passes when the procedure
returns normally and its postcondition is satisfied. A test fails when the
procedure returns normally and its postcondition is violated. A test errors when
the procedure is ill-formed for test execution, panics, requires unavailable
authority, or cannot be invoked by the generated harness.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 9.6.6 Lowering

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: lowering.TestHarnessGeneration
kind: lowering-rule
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: driver.tests
applies-to: testing, lowering, build-output, procedures, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines source-native test target resolution, discovery, and ephemeral harness generation for uv test.
-->

`#test` does not lower into production program artifacts.

TestArg = ⊥ | s where s is the optional positional argument to `uv test`.

HostPath(s) ⇔ ResolveHostPath(CurrentDirectory, s) ⇓ p ∧ exists(p)

TestInput(⊥) = CurrentDirectory
TestInput(s) = p  if HostPath(s) ∧ ResolveHostPath(CurrentDirectory, s) ⇓ p
TestInput(s) = CurrentDirectory  if ¬ HostPath(s)

TestRoot(arg) = FindProjectRoot(TestInput(arg))

TestsPrefix(A) = A.name :: `Tests`
TestBearing(A) ⇔ ∃ m ∈ A.modules. Prefix(path(m), TestsPrefix(A))
TestAssemblies(P) = [A ∈ P.assemblies | TestBearing(A)]

TestScope ::= AllTests | AssemblyTests(A) | ModuleTests(q) | SourceFileTests(f) | DirectoryTests(d)

ResolveTestTarget(P, ⊥) = AllTests
ResolveTestTarget(P, s) = SourceFileTests(p)
  if HostPath(s) ∧ ResolveHostPath(CurrentDirectory, s) ⇓ p ∧ File(p)
ResolveTestTarget(P, s) = AllTests
  if HostPath(s) ∧ ResolveHostPath(CurrentDirectory, s) ⇓ p ∧ Dir(p) ∧ p = P.root
ResolveTestTarget(P, s) = DirectoryTests(p)
  if HostPath(s) ∧ ResolveHostPath(CurrentDirectory, s) ⇓ p ∧ Dir(p) ∧ p ≠ P.root
ResolveTestTarget(P, s) = AssemblyTests(A)
  if ¬ HostPath(s) ∧ A ∈ P.assemblies ∧ A.name = s
ResolveTestTarget(P, s) = ModuleTests(q)
  if ¬ HostPath(s) ∧ ParseModulePath(s) ⇓ q ∧ ∃ m ∈ ModuleList(P). path(m) = q
ResolveTestTarget(P, s) ⇑ Code(Test-Target-Err) otherwise

SelectedTests(P, AllTests) =
  [proc | A ∈ TestAssemblies(P), proc ∈ TestProceduresUnder(A, TestsPrefix(A))]
SelectedTests(P, AssemblyTests(A)) =
  [proc | proc ∈ TestProceduresUnder(A, TestsPrefix(A))]
SelectedTests(P, ModuleTests(q)) =
  [proc | proc ∈ TestProceduresUnder(OwnerAssembly(P, q), q)]
SelectedTests(P, SourceFileTests(f)) =
  [proc | proc ∈ TestProceduresInFile(P, f) ∧ InTestsSubtree(P, proc)]
SelectedTests(P, DirectoryTests(d)) =
  [proc | proc ∈ TestProceduresUnderDirectory(P, d) ∧ InTestsSubtree(P, proc)]

For each selected assembly A represented in SelectedTests(P, scope), `uv test`
generates an ephemeral harness in A's build output directory, compiles
AssemblyProject(P, A) with that harness entrypoint, and invokes the selected
tests for A in deterministic order.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TestDiscoveryOrder
kind: formal-definition
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: driver.tests
applies-to: testing, deterministic-order, modules, procedures, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines deterministic discovery order and stable identity for source-native tests.
-->

Discovery order is module path, file order, declaration span, then
fully-qualified procedure symbol. The fully-qualified procedure path is the
stable test identity. `name: "..."` is a display label.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

## 10. Permissions and Binding State

### 10.1 Permission Forms

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

-->

#### 10.1.1 Syntax

```ebnf
permission         ::= "const" | "unique" | "shared"
receiver_shorthand ::= "~" | "~!" | "~%"
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

owner: parser.permissions

-->

Permission qualifiers appear in `type ::= permission? non_permission_type refinement_clause?`. Receiver shorthand forms map to receiver permissions as defined by the parser and AST rules in Chapter 5.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 10.1.2 Parsing

-->

Permission tokens are parsed by `ParsePermOpt` in type position and by `ParseReceiver` in receiver position.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: normative-requirement
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.permissions

-->

The canonical `ParseReceiver` rules are the token-gated parsing rules in §15.2.2. This section owns only the permission-specific token inventory consumed by those rules.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 10.1.3 AST Representation / Form

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.PermissionAstForms
kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.permissions
applies-to: parsing, ast, permissions, receivers, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines permission AST forms for permissions, permission-qualified types, and receiver shorthands.
-->

Permission syntax lowers into the following AST forms:

- `Perm` ranges over `{const, unique, shared}`.
- `TypePerm(perm, base)`
- `ReceiverShorthand(perm)`

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

-->

A permission-qualified type is represented as `TypePerm(P, T)` where `P ∈ Perm` and `T` is the unqualified base type.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 10.1.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.PermissionQualifierSemantics
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.permissions
applies-to: semantic-analysis, permissions, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines a permission as a type qualifier governing access, mutation, and aliasing, with const as the default.
-->

**Permission.** A type qualifier governing access, mutation, and aliasing of data referenced by a binding. When no permission is specified, `const` is the default.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.PermissionRegimesDistinct
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.permissions
applies-to: semantic-analysis, permissions, type-system, diagnostics, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires const, shared, and unique to be distinct permission regimes without implicit subtype or coercion ordering.
-->

**Permission Regimes.** `const`, `shared`, and `unique` are distinct permission regimes. They are not ordered by implicit subtype or coercion.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.PermissionRegimeProperties
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.permissions
applies-to: semantic-analysis, permissions, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines read, write, aliasing, and synchronization properties of permission regimes.
-->

The following properties define the regimes:

| Permission | Read | Write | Aliasing  | Synchronization |
| :--------- | :--- | :---- | :-------- | :-------------- |
| `const`    | Yes  | No    | Unlimited | N/A             |
| `shared`   | Yes  | Yes   | Aliasable | Key-mediated    |
| `unique`   | Yes  | Yes   | Exclusive | None            |

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.PermissionRegimeConstraints
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.permissions
applies-to: semantic-analysis, permissions, mutation, ownership, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines const mutation prohibition and states that unique/shared access does not imply cleanup responsibility.
-->

Additional regime-specific constraints:

- `const` forbids mutation through the qualified path.
- `unique` grants exclusive read-write access and does not imply cleanup responsibility.
- `shared` grants synchronized access and does not imply cleanup responsibility.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.SharedPermissionOperationMatrix
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.permissions
applies-to: semantic-analysis, permissions, receivers, key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines permitted shared operations and required key modes.
-->

For `shared`, the permitted operations are:

| Operation                   | Permitted | Key Mode  |
| :-------------------------- | :-------- | :-------- |
| Field read                  | Yes       | Read key  |
| Field mutation              | Yes       | Write key |
| Method call (`~` receiver)  | Yes       | Read key  |
| Method call (`~%` receiver) | Yes       | Write key |
| Method call (`~!` receiver) | No        | N/A       |

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 10.1.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: conformance.PermissionDynamicSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: runtime.permissions
applies-to: runtime, permissions, key-system, oracle.behavior, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines runtime behavior of const, unique, and shared permission qualifiers.
-->

Permissions do not change the represented value of the underlying object.

- `const` introduces no additional runtime action.
- `unique` introduces no implicit cleanup transfer.
- `shared` access performs implicit key acquisition and release as defined by the key system in Chapter 19.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-definition

aliases(p_1, p_2) ⇔ storage(p_1) ∩ storage(p_2) ≠ ∅

**Exclusivity Invariant.**

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

∀ p_1, p_2 ∈ Paths. (perm(p_1) = `unique` ∧ overlaps(p_1, p_2)) ⇒ p_1 = p_2

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

#### 10.3.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.UniqueBindingActivityStates
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.permissions
applies-to: semantic-analysis, permissions, unique-access, binding-state, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Active and Inactive states for unique-permission bindings and their permitted operations.
-->

A binding `b` with `unique` permission exists in one of two states:

| State    | Definition                                              | Operations Permitted        |
| :------- | :------------------------------------------------------ | :-------------------------- |
| Active   | No suspended admissible uses of `b` are live            | Read, write, move           |
| Inactive | A non-consuming admissible use of `b` is currently live | No direct operations on `b` |

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Inactive-Enter
kind: formal-rule
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.permissions
applies-to: semantic-analysis, permissions, unique-access, binding-state, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines formal rule Inactive-Enter from rules.BindingActivityStates.
labels: Inactive-Enter
-->

**(Inactive-Enter)**
b : `unique` T    b is Active    non-consuming admissible use of b begins
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
b becomes Inactive

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: Inactive-Exit
kind: formal-rule
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.permissions
applies-to: semantic-analysis, permissions, unique-access, binding-state, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines formal rule Inactive-Exit from rules.BindingActivityStates.
labels: Inactive-Exit
-->

**(Inactive-Exit)**
b is Inactive    all live non-consuming admissible uses of b end
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
b becomes Active with `unique` permission preserved

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

summary: Requires the original unique binding to be unusable while inactive.
-->

#### 10.3.5 Dynamic Semantics

During the inactive period, the original `unique` binding MUST NOT be read, written, or moved.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

-->

Entering or exiting the inactive state does not create a `shared` or `const` alias. It suspends direct use of the `unique` binding while the admissible use remains live.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

The transition back to `Active` occurs deterministically when the admissible-use scope ends.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

### 11.2 Using Declarations

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.UsingDeclarationSyntax
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser
applies-to: parsing, semantic-analysis, modules, using, name-resolution, visibility, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines using declaration grammar and its module_path dependency.
-->

#### 11.2.1 Syntax

```ebnf
using_decl      ::= attribute_list? visibility? "using" using_clause
using_clause    ::= module_path "::" identifier ("as" identifier)?
                  | module_path "::" using_list
                  | module_path "::" "*"
using_list      ::= "{" using_specifier ("," using_specifier)* "}"
using_specifier ::= identifier ("as" identifier)?
```

`module_path` is defined by §11.5.1.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 11.2.3 AST Representation / Form

`UsingDecl` is a top-level AST item with one of three clause forms.

UsingDecl = ⟨attrs_opt, vis, clause, span, doc⟩

UsingClause ∈ {
  UsingItem = ⟨module_path, name, alias_opt⟩,
  UsingList = ⟨module_path, specs⟩,
  UsingWildcard = ⟨module_path⟩
}

UsingSpec = ⟨name, alias_opt⟩    name ∈ identifier

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 11.2.4 Static Semantics

Using-path resolution and import coverage are defined by §11.5.4. Accessibility is defined by Chapter 7. This section defines the bindings produced by each `using` form.

#### 11.2.5 Dynamic Semantics

`using` declarations are compile-time only. They introduce no runtime action.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 11.2.6 Lowering

`using` declarations introduce no construct-specific lowering. Their effects are exhausted by name binding.

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: diagnostics.UsingDeclarations

#### 11.2.7 Diagnostics

| Code         | Severity | Detection    | Condition                                        |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `E-MOD-1204` | Error    | Compile-time | Using path does not resolve to an item           |
| `E-MOD-1205` | Error    | Compile-time | Attempt to `public using` a non-public item      |
| `E-MOD-1206` | Error    | Compile-time | Duplicate item in a `using` list                 |
| `W-MOD-1201` | Warning  | Compile-time | Wildcard `using` in a module exposing public API |

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

### 11.3 Static Declarations

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: grammar

strength: required
owner: parser

-->

#### 11.3.1 Syntax

```ebnf
static_decl  ::= attribute_list? visibility? ("let" | "var") binding_decl
binding_decl ::= pattern (":" type)? binding_op expression
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

This chapter uses `StaticDecl` for top-level `let` and `var` items.

`StaticDecl` is parsed by the item parser. Pattern and initializer parsing reuse the shared binding parser.

ViewPaths(Ms) = [M.path | M ∈ Ms]
ViewAssembly(A, P, Ms) =
 A[modules := ViewPaths(Ms)]  if A.name = P.assembly.name
 A                            otherwise

summary: Defines visible assemblies, public API status, visible module paths, and visible module names.
-->

VisibleAssemblies(m) = {AsmOfModule(m)} ∪ {AsmOfPath(p) | p ∈ ImportPaths(m)}
PublicAPI(m) ⇔ ∃ it ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items. Vis(it) = `public`
VisibleModulePaths(m) = { p | p ∈ AllModulePaths(P) ∧ AsmOfPath(p) ∈ VisibleAssemblies(m) }
AllModuleNames = { StringOfPath(p) | p ∈ AllModulePaths(P) }
VisibleModuleNames(m) = { StringOfPath(p) | p ∈ VisibleModulePaths(m) }
ModulePaths = VisibleModulePaths(m)
ModuleNames = VisibleModuleNames(m)
Alias = AliasMap(m)
AllModules = AllModulePaths(P)

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.AstTraversalNodeHelpers
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, type-references, value-references, diagnostics, lowering, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines AST node extraction and subnode traversal helpers.
-->

Elems(v) =
 {v}    if v ∈ ASTNode
 {x | x ∈ v ∧ x ∈ ASTNode}    if v ∈ [_]
 ∅    if v = ⊥
 ∅    otherwise

Child(x, y) ⇔ ∃ C, a_1, …, a_k. x = C(a_1, …, a_k) ∧ y ∈ ⋃_{i=1}^k Elems(a_i)
E_child = { (x, y) | Child(x, y) }
Subnode(x, y) ⇔ x = y ∨ Γ ⊢ Reachable(x, y, E_child)

ExprNodes(P, m) = { e | e ∈ Expr ∧ Subnode(ASTModule(P, m), e) }
PatNodes(P, m) = { p | p ∈ Pattern ∧ Subnode(ASTModule(P, m), p) }
ExprNodesOf(x) = { e | e ∈ Expr ∧ Subnode(x, e) }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.EnumVariantTypeSets
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, type-references, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines type-position extraction from enum variant payloads.
-->

VariantPayloadTypeSet(⊥) = ∅
VariantPayloadTypeSet(TuplePayload(tys)) = { t | t ∈ tys }
VariantPayloadTypeSet(RecordPayload(fields)) = { t | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, boundary, name, init_opt, span, doc_opt. FieldDecl(attrs_opt, vis, boundary, name, t, init_opt, span, doc_opt) ∈ fields }
EnumVariantTypeSet(variants) = { t | ∃ name, payload_opt, disc_opt, span, doc_opt. VariantDecl(name, payload_opt, disc_opt, span, doc_opt) ∈ variants ∧ t ∈ VariantPayloadTypeSet(payload_opt) }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.GeneralTypePositionSetHelpers
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, type-references, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines reusable helper sets for optional types, parameter types, receiver types, and class path types.
-->

TypeOptSet(⊥) = ∅
TypeOptSet(T) = {T}
ParamTypeSet(params) = { t | ∃ mode, name. ⟨mode, name, t⟩ ∈ params }
RecvTypeSet(ReceiverExplicit(_, t)) = {t}
RecvTypeSet(ReceiverShorthand(_)) = ∅
ClassPathTypeSet(paths) = { TypePath(p) | p ∈ paths }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.RecordMemberTypeSets
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, type-references, records, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines type-position extraction from record fields and methods.
-->

RecordFieldTypeSet(members) = { t | ∃ attrs, vis, boundary, name, init, span, doc. FieldDecl(attrs, vis, boundary, name, t, init, span, doc) ∈ members }
RecordMethodRecvTypes(members) = { t | ∃ attrs, vis, ov, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc. MethodDecl(attrs, vis, ov, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc) ∈ members ∧ t ∈ RecvTypeSet(recv) }
RecordMethodParamTypes(members) = { t | ∃ attrs, vis, ov, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc. MethodDecl(attrs, vis, ov, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc) ∈ members ∧ t ∈ ParamTypeSet(params) }
RecordMethodRetTypes(members) = { t | ∃ attrs, vis, ov, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc. MethodDecl(attrs, vis, ov, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc) ∈ members ∧ t ∈ TypeOptSet(ret) }
RecordMemberTypeSet(members) = RecordFieldTypeSet(members) ∪ RecordMethodRecvTypes(members) ∪ RecordMethodParamTypes(members) ∪ RecordMethodRetTypes(members)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ClassItemTypeSets

-->

ClassFieldTypeSet(items) = { t | ∃ attrs, vis, boundary, name, span, doc. ClassFieldDecl(attrs, vis, boundary, name, t, span, doc) ∈ items }
ClassMethodRecvTypes(items) = { t | ∃ attrs, vis, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc. ClassMethodDecl(attrs, vis, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc) ∈ items ∧ t ∈ RecvTypeSet(recv) }
ClassMethodParamTypes(items) = { t | ∃ attrs, vis, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc. ClassMethodDecl(attrs, vis, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc) ∈ items ∧ t ∈ ParamTypeSet(params) }
ClassMethodRetTypes(items) = { t | ∃ attrs, vis, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc. ClassMethodDecl(attrs, vis, name, gen_params, recv, params, ret, contract, body, span, doc) ∈ items ∧ t ∈ TypeOptSet(ret) }
ClassItemTypeSet(items) = ClassFieldTypeSet(items) ∪ ClassMethodRecvTypes(items) ∪ ClassMethodParamTypes(items) ∪ ClassMethodRetTypes(items)

owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, type-references, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines type-position extraction from module-scope declarations.
-->

TypePos_Static(P, m) = { t | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, mut, bind, span, doc. StaticDecl(attrs_opt, vis, mut, bind, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ bind.type_opt = t ∧ t ≠ ⊥ }
TypePos_Proc(P, m) = { t | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, params, return_type_opt, contract_opt, body, span, doc. ProcedureDecl(attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, params, return_type_opt, contract_opt, body, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ t ∈ (ParamTypeSet(params) ∪ TypeOptSet(return_type_opt)) }
TypePos_Record(P, m) = { t | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, members, invariant_opt, span, doc. RecordDecl(attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, members, invariant_opt, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ t ∈ (ClassPathTypeSet(impls) ∪ RecordMemberTypeSet(members)) }
TypePos_Enum(P, m) = { t | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, variants, invariant_opt, span, doc. EnumDecl(attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, variants, invariant_opt, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ t ∈ (ClassPathTypeSet(impls) ∪ EnumVariantTypeSet(variants)) }
TypePos_Modal(P, m) = { t | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, states, invariant_opt, span, doc. ModalDecl(attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, states, invariant_opt, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ t ∈ ClassPathTypeSet(impls) }
TypePos_Class(P, m) = { t | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, modal, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, supers, items, span, doc. ClassDecl(attrs_opt, vis, modal, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, supers, items, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ t ∈ (ClassPathTypeSet(supers) ∪ ClassItemTypeSet(items)) }
TypePos_Alias(P, m) = { t | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, ty, span, doc. TypeAliasDecl(attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, ty, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ t = ty }
TypePositions(P, m) = TypePos_Static(P, m) ∪ TypePos_Proc(P, m) ∪ TypePos_Record(P, m) ∪ TypePos_Enum(P, m) ∪ TypePos_Modal(P, m) ∪ TypePos_Class(P, m) ∪ TypePos_Alias(P, m)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TypePositionExpressions
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, type-references, value-references, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines expressions appearing in type positions for dependency analysis.
-->

ArraySizeExprs(P, m) = { e | ∃ elem. TypeArray(elem, e) ∈ TypePositions(P, m) }
EnumDiscriminantExprs(P, m) = { e | ∃ attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, variants, invariant_opt, span, doc. EnumDecl(attrs_opt, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, variants, invariant_opt, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ ∃ v. v = VariantDecl(_, _, e, _, _) ∈ variants ∧ e ≠ ⊥ }
TypePosExprs(P, m) = ArraySizeExprs(P, m) ∪ EnumDiscriminantExprs(P, m)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TypeDeps
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, type-references, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines type dependencies for a module from type positions, patterns, expressions, and type-position expressions.
-->

TypeDeps(P, m) = { n | ∃ t ∈ TypePositions(P, m). Γ ⊢ TypeRefsTy(t, env_m) ⇓ T ∧ n ∈ T } ∪ { n | ∃ p ∈ PatNodes(P, m). Γ ⊢ TypeRefsPat(p, env_m) ⇓ T ∧ n ∈ T } ∪ { n | ∃ e ∈ (ExprNodes(P, m) ∪ TypePosExprs(P, m)). Γ ⊢ TypeRefsExpr(e, env_m) ⇓ T ∧ n ∈ T }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ValueDependencyExpressionSets
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, value-references, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines expression sets considered for eager and lazy value dependencies.
-->

StaticInitExprs(P, m) = { init | ∃ attrs, vis, mut, bind, span, doc. StaticDecl(attrs, vis, mut, bind, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ bind.init = init }
RecordFieldInitExprs(P, m) = { init | ∃ attrs, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, members, invariant_opt, span, doc. RecordDecl(attrs, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, members, invariant_opt, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ ∃ f. f = FieldDecl(_, _, _, _, _, init, _, _) ∈ members ∧ init ≠ ⊥ }
ProcBodies(P, m) = { body | ∃ attrs, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, params, ret_opt, contract_opt, body, span, doc. ProcedureDecl(attrs, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, params, ret_opt, contract_opt, body, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items }
RecordMethodBodies(P, m) = { body | ∃ attrs, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, members, invariant_opt, span, doc. RecordDecl(attrs, vis, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, impls, members, invariant_opt, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ ∃ md. md = MethodDecl(_, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, body, _, _) ∈ members }
ClassMethodBodies(P, m) = { body | ∃ attrs, vis, modal, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, supers, items, span, doc. ClassDecl(attrs, vis, modal, name, gen_params_opt, predicate_clause_opt, supers, items, span, doc) ∈ ASTModule(P, m).items ∧ ∃ md. md = ClassMethodDecl(_, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, body, _, _) ∈ items ∧ body ≠ ⊥ }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ValueDepsEagerLazy
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, value-references, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines eager and lazy value dependencies for a module.
-->

ValueDepsEager(P, m) = { n | ∃ e ∈ StaticInitExprs(P, m). Γ ⊢ ValueRefs(e, env_m) ⇓ V ∧ n ∈ V }
ValueDepsLazy(P, m) = { n | ∃ e ∈ RecordFieldInitExprs(P, m) ∪ ⋃_{b ∈ (ProcBodies(P, m) ∪ RecordMethodBodies(P, m) ∪ ClassMethodBodies(P, m))} ExprNodesOf(b). Γ ⊢ ValueRefs(e, env_m) ⇓ V ∧ n ∈ V }

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.ModuleDependencyGraphs
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.modules
applies-to: semantic-analysis, modules, initialization, dependencies, type-references, value-references, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines module dependency graph vertices, edge sets, full graph, and eager-initializer graph.
-->

V = AllModules
E_type = {(m, n) | n ∈ TypeDeps(P, m)}
E_val^{eager} = {(m, n) | n ∈ ValueDepsEager(P, m)}
E_val^{lazy} = {(m, n) | n ∈ ValueDepsLazy(P, m)}

G = ⟨V, E_type, E_val^{eager}, E_val^{lazy}⟩
G_e = ⟨V, E_val^{eager}⟩

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: WF-Acyclic-Eager
kind: formal-rule
phase: semantic-analysis

labels: WF-Acyclic-Eager
-->

**(WF-Acyclic-Eager)**
∀ v ∈ V. ¬ Reachable(v, v, E_val^{eager})
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ G_e : DAG

## 12. Concrete Data Types

### 12.1 Primitive Types

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.PrimitiveTypeSyntax
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.types
applies-to: parsing, semantic-analysis, runtime, lowering, primitive-types, numeric-types, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines primitive type grammar.
-->

#### 12.1.1 Syntax

```ebnf
primitive_type  ::= signed_int_type
                  | unsigned_int_type
                  | float_type
                  | "bool"
                  | "char"
                  | "(" ")"
                  | "!"
signed_int_type ::= "i8" | "i16" | "i32" | "i64" | "i128" | "isize"
unsigned_int_type ::= "u8" | "u16" | "u32" | "u64" | "u128" | "usize"
float_type      ::= "f16" | "f32" | "f64"
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.PrimitiveFloatRepresentation
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types.primitive
applies-to: parsing, semantic-analysis, runtime, lowering, primitive-types, numeric-types, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines primitive float formats, encodings, canonical NaN behavior, and IEEE bit extraction.
-->

FloatFormat("f16") = `binary16`    FloatFormat("f32") = `binary32`    FloatFormat("f64") = `binary64`
FloatBitWidth("f16") = 16    FloatBitWidth("f32") = 32    FloatBitWidth("f64") = 64
FloatValueSet(t) = { v | v is a value representable by IEEE 754-2019 format FloatFormat(t) }
IEEE754Encode(t, v) = bits ⇔ v ∈ FloatValueSet(t) ∧ bits ∈ [0, 2^{FloatBitWidth(t)} - 1] ∧ ((v is NaN in IEEE 754-2019 format FloatFormat(t) ∧ bits = CanonicalNaNBits(t)) ∨ (v is not NaN in IEEE 754-2019 format FloatFormat(t) ∧ bits is the IEEE 754-2019 encoding of v in format FloatFormat(t)))
CanonicalNaNBits("f16") = 0x7E00    CanonicalNaNBits("f32") = 0x7FC00000    CanonicalNaNBits("f64") = 0x7FF8000000000000
CanonicalNaN(t) = v ⇔ IEEE754Encode(t, v) = CanonicalNaNBits(t)
NonNaNValueSet(t) = { v ∈ FloatValueSet(t) | IEEE754Encode(t, v) ≠ CanonicalNaNBits(t) }
LSB(n) = n mod 2
EvenSignificandLSB(t, v) ⇔ LSB(IEEE754Encode(t, v)) = 0
IEEE754Bits(t, v) = bits ⇔ v ∈ FloatValueSet(t) ∧ IEEE754Encode(t, v) = bits

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

kind: formal-definition

-->

IntWidth(`i8`) = 8    IntWidth(`i16`) = 16    IntWidth(`i32`) = 32    IntWidth(`i64`) = 64    IntWidth(`i128`) = 128
IntWidth(`u8`) = 8    IntWidth(`u16`) = 16    IntWidth(`u32`) = 32    IntWidth(`u64`) = 64    IntWidth(`u128`) = 128
IntWidth(`isize`) = 8 × PointerSize    IntWidth(`usize`) = 8 × PointerSize

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.PrimitiveRangeOf
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types.primitive
applies-to: semantic-analysis, primitive-types, numeric-types, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines numeric primitive ranges and the InRange predicate.
-->

RangeOf : PrimitiveTypeName ⇀ ℘(ℝ)
RangeOf(t) = [-2^{w-1}, 2^{w-1} - 1] if t ∈ SignedIntTypes ∧ w = IntWidth(t)
RangeOf(t) = [0, 2^{w} - 1] if t ∈ UnsignedIntTypes ∧ w = IntWidth(t)
RangeOf(t) undefined otherwise
InRange(v, T) ⇔ v ∈ RangeOf(T)

summary: Defines runtime ValueType mappings for primitive values.

#### 12.1.5 Dynamic Semantics

ValueType(IntVal(t, x)) = TypePrim(t)
ValueType(FloatVal(t, v)) = TypePrim(t)
ValueType(v) = TypePrim("bool") ⇔ ∃ b. v = BoolVal(b)
ValueType(v) = TypePrim("char") ⇔ ∃ u. v = CharVal(u)
ValueType(BoolVal(true)) = TypePrim("bool")
ValueType(BoolVal(false)) = TypePrim("bool")
ValueType(CharVal(u)) = TypePrim("char")
ValueType(UnitVal) = TypePrim("()")

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.PrimitiveValueBits
kind: formal-definition
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: codegen
applies-to: lowering, primitive-types, numeric-types, abi, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines lowering bit encodings for primitive values.
-->

#### 12.1.6 Lowering

ValueBits(TypePrim("bool"), v) = bits ⇔ (v = BoolVal(true) ∧ bits = [0x01]) ∨ (v = BoolVal(false) ∧ bits = [0x00])
ValueBits(TypePrim("char"), v) = bits ⇔ v = CharVal(u) ∧ LEBytes(u, 4) = bits
ValueBits(TypePrim("()"), v) = bits ⇔ v = UnitVal ∧ bits = []
ValueBits(TypePrim(t), v) = bits ⇔ t ∈ IntTypes ∧ v = IntVal(t, x) ∧ LEBytes(x, sizeof(TypePrim(t))) = bits
ValueBits(TypePrim(t), v) = bits ⇔ t ∈ FloatTypes ∧ v = FloatVal(t, x) ∧ LEBytes(IEEE754Bits(t, x), sizeof(TypePrim(t))) = bits

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

#### 12.2.1 Syntax

```ebnf
tuple_type       ::= "(" ")"
                   | "(" type ";)"
                   | "(" type ("," type)+ trailing_comma? ")"
tuple_expr       ::= "(" ")"
                   | "(" expr ";)"
                   | "(" expr ("," expr)+ trailing_comma? ")"
tuple_projection ::= postfix_expr "." int_literal
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: req.TupleSingletonCommaIllFormed
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.types
applies-to: parsing, tuples, diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires singleton comma tuple type and expression forms to be ill-formed, and trailing comma to mean continuation only.
-->

The singleton comma forms `("(" type ",)")` and `("(" expr ",)")` are ill-formed. A trailing comma denotes continuation only and does not create a one-element tuple.

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TupleScanDelimiterDeltas
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types.tuples
applies-to: parsing, semantic-analysis, runtime, lowering, tuples, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines tuple scan delimiter depth deltas.
-->

ParenDelta(Punctuator("(")) = 1
ParenDelta(Punctuator(")")) = -1
ParenDelta(t) = 0 if t.kind ∉ {Punctuator("("), Punctuator(")")}

BracketDelta(Punctuator("[")) = 1
BracketDelta(Punctuator("]")) = -1
BracketDelta(t) = 0 if t.kind ∉ {Punctuator("["), Punctuator("]")}

BraceDelta(Punctuator("{")) = 1
BraceDelta(Punctuator("}")) = -1
BraceDelta(t) = 0 if t.kind ∉ {Punctuator("{"), Punctuator("}")}

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TupleScanDepthAndStep
kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.types
applies-to: parsing, tuples, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines tuple scan depth representation and scan-step update.
-->

TupleScanDepth = ⟨p, q, r⟩ where p, q, r ∈ Nat
TupleScan(P, d) ⇓ b ⇔ TupleScan(P, ⟨d, 0, 0⟩) ⇓ b
TupleScanStep(⟨p, q, r⟩, t) = ⟨p + ParenDelta(t), max(0, q + BracketDelta(t)), max(0, r + BraceDelta(t))⟩

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.TupleScanPredicates
kind: formal-definition
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.types
applies-to: parsing, tuples, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines tuple scan separator, singleton-comma, end-paren, and advancement predicates.
-->

TupleScanOuterSep(⟨p, q, r⟩) ⇔ p = 1 ∧ q = 0 ∧ r = 0
TupleScanSingletonComma(P) ⇔ Tok(P) = Punctuator(",") ∧ IsPunc(Tok(SkipNL(Advance(P))), ")")
TupleScanEndParen(P, ⟨p, q, r⟩) ⇔ Tok(P) = Punctuator(")") ∧ p = 1
TupleScanSep(P, D) ⇔ Tok(P) ∈ {Punctuator(","), Punctuator(";")} ∧ TupleScanOuterSep(D)
TupleScanAdvance(P, D) ⇔ Tok(P) ≠ EOF ∧ ¬ TupleScanEndParen(P, D) ∧ ¬ TupleScanSep(P, D)

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 12.2.7 Diagnostics

| Code         | Severity | Detection    | Condition                                                  |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `E-TYP-1801` | Error    | Compile-time | Tuple index out of bounds                                  |
| `E-TYP-1802` | Error    | Compile-time | Tuple index is not a compile-time constant integer literal |
| `E-TYP-1803` | Error    | Compile-time | Tuple arity mismatch in assignment or pattern              |
| `E-SEM-2524` | Error    | Compile-time | Tuple access on non-tuple                                  |

### 12.3 Arrays

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.ArraySyntax
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: parser.types
applies-to: parsing, semantic-analysis, runtime, lowering, arrays, indexing, dynamic-verification, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines array type, array expression, array segment, and index expression grammar.
-->

#### 12.3.1 Syntax

```ebnf
array_type    ::= "[" type ";" expr "]"
array_expr    ::= "[" array_segment_list? "]"
array_segment_list ::= array_segment ("," array_segment)*
array_segment ::= expr | expr ";" expr
index_expr    ::= postfix_expr "[" expr "]"
```

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 12.3.3 AST Representation / Form

TypeArray = ⟨elem, size_expr⟩ where elem ∈ Type ∧ size_expr ∈ Expr
ArraySegment = ArrayElemSegment(value) | ArrayRepeatSegment(value, count) where value ∈ Expr ∧ count ∈ Expr
ArrayExpr = ⟨segments⟩ where segments ∈ [ArraySegment]

#### 12.3.4 Static Semantics

ConstIndex(e) ⇔ ∃ n. Γ ⊢ ConstLen(e) ⇓ n

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.IndexUsizeExpr
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types.arrays
applies-to: semantic-analysis, arrays, slices, indexing, integer-literals, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines contextual usize checking for scalar array and slice index expressions.
-->

IndexUsizeExpr(e) ⇔ (Γ ⊢ e : TypePrim("usize")) ∨ (e = Literal(lit) ∧ lit.kind = IntLiteral ∧ IntSuffix(lit) = ⊥ ∧ InRange(IntValue(lit), "usize"))

`IndexUsizeExpr` is a contextual integer-literal checking relation for array and slice index positions. It accepts an unsuffixed integer literal that fits `usize` without changing the standalone synthesized type of that literal. It MUST NOT admit explicitly suffixed non-`usize` literals, and it MUST NOT convert non-literal expressions; non-literal index expressions must already type as `TypePrim("usize")`.

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 12.3.7 Diagnostics

Diagnostics are defined for non-constant array indexing outside `#dynamic` scope, out-of-bounds constant indices, and non-`usize` array indices. Runtime out-of-bounds behavior for dynamic indices is defined by the panic behavior of `EvalSigma-Index-OOB`.

id: def.RangeIndexType
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required

summary: Defines the range index types accepted for slicing.
-->

#### 12.4.4 Static Semantics

RangeIndexType(T_r) ⇔ T_r = TypeRange(TypePrim("usize")) ∨ T_r = TypeRangeInclusive(TypePrim("usize")) ∨ T_r = TypeRangeFrom(TypePrim("usize")) ∨ T_r = TypeRangeTo(TypePrim("usize")) ∨ T_r = TypeRangeToInclusive(TypePrim("usize")) ∨ T_r = TypeRangeFull

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.RangeIndexExpr
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: checker.types.slices
applies-to: semantic-analysis, arrays, slices, indexing, ranges, integer-literals, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines contextual range-bound checking for array and slice range indexing.
-->

RangeIndexExpr(r) ⇔ (Γ; R; L ⊢ r : Range ∧ RangeIndexType(ExprType(r))) ∨ r = Range(`Full`, ⊥, ⊥) ∨ (r = Range(`To`, ⊥, e) ∧ IndexUsizeExpr(e)) ∨ (r = Range(`ToInclusive`, ⊥, e) ∧ IndexUsizeExpr(e)) ∨ (r = Range(`From`, e, ⊥) ∧ IndexUsizeExpr(e)) ∨ (r = Range(`Exclusive`, e_1, e_2) ∧ IndexUsizeExpr(e_1) ∧ IndexUsizeExpr(e_2)) ∨ (r = Range(`Inclusive`, e_1, e_2) ∧ IndexUsizeExpr(e_1) ∧ IndexUsizeExpr(e_2))

`RangeIndexExpr` is a contextual array/slice slicing relation. It preserves already-typed `usize` range carriers and additionally accepts direct range expressions whose explicit bounds satisfy `IndexUsizeExpr`. Standalone range expressions still synthesize their ordinary range types under §12.5.4.

applies-to: runtime, slices, indexing, ranges, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines slice runtime length and index value lookup helpers.
-->

Len(SliceValue(v, r)) = end - start    (SliceBounds(r, Len(v)) = (start, end))

phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: codegen
applies-to: parsing, semantic-analysis, runtime, lowering, slices, indexing, ranges, diagnostics, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines lowering bit encoding for slice values.
-->

ValueBits(TypeSlice(T), SliceValue(v, r)) = bits ⇔ SliceBounds(r, Len(v)) = (start, end) ∧ n = end - start ∧ ∃ addr. ValueBits(TypeRawPtr(`imm`, T), RawPtr(`imm`, addr)) = b_ptr ∧ ValueBits(TypePrim("usize"), IntVal("usize", n)) = b_len ∧ bits = b_ptr ++ b_len

-->

IndexUpdate(SliceValue(v_b, r), i, v_e) = SliceValue(v_b', r)    (SliceBounds(r, Len(v_b)) = (start, end) ∧ 0 ≤ i < end - start ∧ IndexUpdate(v_b, start + i, v_e) = v_b')

-->

Direct slice indexing follows the same scalar-indexing model as array indexing. Diagnostics are defined for non-`usize` slice indices and non-indexable bases. Runtime slice-bounds failures panic through `EvalSigma-Index-OOB` for scalar indexing and `EvalSigma-Index-Range-OOB` for slicing.
