#### 19.5.5 Dynamic Semantics

**Entry Rule**

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.ExecSigma-KeyBlock-Speculative
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Executes a speculative key block by entering the speculative loop with zero retries.
labels: ExecSigma-KeyBlock-Speculative
-->
**(ExecSigma-KeyBlock-Speculative)**
kind = SpeculativeWrite    retries = 0
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ExecSigma(KeyBlockStmt(attrs_opt, kind, paths, mode, options, body, span), σ) ⇓ SpecLoop(paths, mode, body, retries, σ)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.19.SpecLoop
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines speculative execution loop semantics for snapshot, body evaluation, write collection, commit, retry, and fallback.
labels: SpecLoop, SnapshotKeyedPaths, CollectWrites, SpeculativeCommit, ApplyWrites, MAX_SPECULATIVE_RETRIES
-->
SpecLoop(paths, mode, body, retries, σ) ⇓ (out, σ') ⇔
  R = SnapshotKeyedPaths(paths, σ) ∧
  Γ ⊢ EvalBlockSigma(body, σ) ⇓ (out_body, σ_1) ∧
  W = CollectWrites(σ, σ_1) ∧
  (SpeculativeCommit(R, W) ⇒ out = out_body ∧ σ' = ApplyWrites(σ, W)) ∧
  (¬SpeculativeCommit(R, W) ∧ retries < MAX_SPECULATIVE_RETRIES ⇒ SpecLoop(paths, mode, body, retries + 1, σ) ⇓ (out, σ')) ∧
  (¬SpeculativeCommit(R, W) ∧ retries = MAX_SPECULATIVE_RETRIES ⇒ Γ ⊢ ExecSigma(KeyBlockStmt(attrs_opt, Write, paths, Write, options, body, span), σ) ⇓ (out, σ'))
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

**State Machine**

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Start
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Starts speculative execution by transitioning to snapshot state.
labels: Spec-Start
-->
**(Spec-Start)**
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecStart(paths, body, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecSnapshot(paths, body, ∅, σ)⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Snapshot
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Reads keyed paths into a speculative read set and transitions to execution state.
labels: Spec-Snapshot
-->
**(Spec-Snapshot)**
∀ p ∈ paths. ReadPath(σ, p) = v_p    R = {(p, v_p) | p ∈ paths}
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecSnapshot(paths, body, ∅, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecExec(body, R, ∅, σ)⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Exec-Ok
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Transitions successful speculative execution to commit state with collected writes.
labels: Spec-Exec-Ok
-->
**(Spec-Exec-Ok)**
Γ ⊢ EvalSpeculative(body, σ, R) ⇓ (Val(v), W, σ')
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecExec(body, R, ∅, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecCommit(R, W, v, σ')⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Exec-Panic
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Transitions panicking speculative execution to speculative panic state.
labels: Spec-Exec-Panic
-->
**(Spec-Exec-Panic)**
Γ ⊢ EvalSpeculative(body, σ, R) ⇓ (Ctrl(Panic), W, σ')
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecExec(body, R, ∅, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecPanic(σ')⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Commit-Success
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Commits speculative writes when the read set still matches current state.
labels: Spec-Commit-Success
-->
**(Spec-Commit-Success)**
∀ (p, v) ∈ R. ReadPath(σ, p) = v    ApplyWrites(σ, W) = σ'
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecCommit(R, W, v, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecDone(v, σ')⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Commit-Fail-Retry
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Retries speculative execution when the read set changed and retry budget remains.
labels: Spec-Commit-Fail-Retry
-->
**(Spec-Commit-Fail-Retry)**
∃ (p, v) ∈ R. ReadPath(σ, p) ≠ v    n < MAX_SPECULATIVE_RETRIES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecCommit(R, W, v, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecRetry(paths(R), body, n + 1, σ)⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Commit-Fail-Fallback
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Falls back to non-speculative execution when the read set changed and retry budget is exhausted.
labels: Spec-Commit-Fail-Fallback
-->
**(Spec-Commit-Fail-Fallback)**
∃ (p, v) ∈ R. ReadPath(σ, p) ≠ v    n ≥ MAX_SPECULATIVE_RETRIES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecCommit(R, W, v, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecFallback(paths(R), body, σ)⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Retry
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Retries speculative execution by returning to snapshot state.
labels: Spec-Retry
-->
**(Spec-Retry)**
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecRetry(paths, body, n, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecSnapshot(paths, body, ∅, σ)⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Spec-Fallback
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Executes speculative fallback by acquiring write keys, evaluating normally, releasing keys, and completing.
labels: Spec-Fallback
-->
**(Spec-Fallback)**
AcquireKey(σ, paths, Write) = σ_k    Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(body, σ_k) ⇓ (Val(v), σ')    ReleaseKey(σ', paths) = σ''
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⟨SpecFallback(paths, body, σ)⟩ → ⟨SpecDone(v, σ'')⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.SpecBlock-Ok
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Evaluates a speculative block successfully when the state machine reaches SpecDone.
labels: SpecBlock-Ok
-->
**(SpecBlock-Ok)**
⟨SpecStart(paths, body, σ)⟩ →* ⟨SpecDone(v, σ')⟩
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ EvalSpecBlock(paths, body, σ) ⇓ (Val(v), σ')
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system

labels: SpecBlock-Panic
-->
**(SpecBlock-Panic)**
⟨SpecStart(paths, body, σ)⟩ →* ⟨SpecPanic(σ')⟩
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ EvalSpecBlock(paths, body, σ) ⇓ (Ctrl(Panic), σ')
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.19.SpeculativeRuntimeHelpers
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines speculative path reading, atomic write application, read-set path extraction, speculative write interception, and retry limit.
labels: ReadPath, ApplyWrites, paths, EvalSpeculative, MAX_SPECULATIVE_RETRIES
-->
ReadPath(σ, p) = v ⇔ evaluate path expression `p` in state `σ`, returning `v`.

ApplyWrites(σ, W) = σ' ⇔ atomically apply all `(p, v) ∈ W` to `σ`.

paths(R) = {p | (p, _) ∈ R}

EvalSpeculative(body, σ, R) ⇓ (out, W, σ') intercepts writes to paths in `paths(R)` and collects them in `W` instead of applying them to `σ`.

`MAX_SPECULATIVE_RETRIES = 8`.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.SpeculativePanicDiscardsWrites
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires panics during speculative execution to discard the write set and propagate the panic.
labels: speculative-panic-discards-writes
-->
If a panic occurs during speculative execution, the write set is discarded and the panic propagates.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.SpeculativeAtomicity
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires speculative snapshots to be observationally atomic and commits to be atomic with respect to overlapping key operations while satisfying SpeculativeCommit.
labels: speculative-snapshot-atomicity, speculative-commit-atomicity, SpeculativeCommit
-->
The snapshot step MUST be observationally equivalent to an atomic snapshot over the keyed set. The commit step MUST be atomic with respect to other key operations on overlapping paths and MUST satisfy `SpeculativeCommit(R, W)`.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.SpeculativeAbstractSemanticsAndFallback
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: permitted
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: States that the speculative state machine is abstract and permits conservative direct fallback when behavior matches an admitted abstract execution.
labels: speculative-abstract-semantics, speculative-direct-fallback
-->
The state machine above is an abstract dynamic semantics.

An implementation MAY conservatively realize `%speculative write ... { ... }` by directly selecting the fallback execution path, provided the resulting observable behavior is the same as some execution admitted by the abstract semantics. Such an implementation need not materialize successful speculative commit states at runtime.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.5.6 Lowering

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.19.SpeculativeIR
kind: formal-definition
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.lowering, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines speculative IR operations for snapshot, validation, commit, retry, and fallback.
labels: SpeculativeIR, SpecSnapshotIR, SpecValidateIR, SpecCommitIR, SpecRetryIR, SpecFallbackIR
-->
SpeculativeIR = {SpecSnapshotIR(paths), SpecValidateIR(paths), SpecCommitIR(paths), SpecRetryIR, SpecFallbackIR}
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Lower-Stmt-KeyBlock-Speculative
kind: formal-rule
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.lowering, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Lowers a speculative key block to speculative loop IR with a non-speculative write-lock fallback.
labels: Lower-Stmt-KeyBlock-Speculative
-->
**(Lower-Stmt-KeyBlock-Speculative)**
kind = SpeculativeWrite    Γ ⊢ LowerKeyPaths(paths) ⇓ Ps    sorted = CanonicalSort(Ps)    Γ ⊢ LowerBlock(body) ⇓ ⟨IR_b, v_b⟩
IR_fallback = SeqIR(SeqIRList([SeqIR(CheckConflict(P_i, Write), AcquireKey(P_i, Write, CurrentScope)) | P_i ∈ sorted]), IR_b, SeqIRList([ReleaseKey(P_i, CurrentScope) | P_i ∈ Reverse(sorted)]))
IR = SpecLoopIR(SpecSnapshotIR(sorted), IR_b, SpecValidateIR(sorted), SpecCommitIR(sorted), SpecRetryIR, SpecFallbackIR(IR_fallback))
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ LowerStmt(KeyBlockStmt(attrs_opt, kind, paths, mode, options, body, span)) ⇓ IR
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

kind: semantic-requirement

#### 19.6.3 AST Representation / Form

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.19.StaticallySafeConditions
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines the sufficient source-condition classes for the conservative StaticallySafe judgment.
labels: StaticallySafe, K-SS-1, K-SS-2, K-SS-3, K-SS-4, K-SS-5, K-SS-6
-->
StaticallySafe(P) is classified by the following source conditions:

| Condition            | Description                                                 | Rule   |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `No escape`          | `shared` value never escapes to another task                | K-SS-1 |
| `Disjoint paths`     | Concurrent accesses target provably disjoint paths          | K-SS-2 |
| `Sequential context` | No `parallel` block encloses the access                     | K-SS-3 |
| `Unique origin`      | Value is `unique` at origin, temporarily viewed as `shared` | K-SS-4 |
| `Dispatch-indexed`   | Access indexed by `dispatch` iteration variable             | K-SS-5 |
| `Speculative-only`   | All accesses occur within speculative blocks with fallback  | K-SS-6 |
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.StaticallySafeSoundProofRequired
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires StaticallySafe to be conservative and false unless the implementation establishes a complete sound proof for the concrete access.
labels: StaticallySafe, static-key-safety-proof
-->
`StaticallySafe(P)` is a conservative compile-time judgment.

The conditions above describe sufficient proof shapes for omitting runtime synchronization.

An implementation MUST treat `StaticallySafe(P)` as false unless it can establish a complete sound proof for the concrete access. Uncertainty is not success.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.6.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.K-Static-Safe
kind: formal-rule
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Marks statically safe key accesses as not requiring runtime synchronization.
labels: K-Static-Safe
-->
**(K-Static-Safe)**
Access(P, M)    StaticallySafe(P)
────────────────────────────────
NoRuntimeSync(P)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.NoRuntimeSyncMeaning
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines NoRuntimeSync and permits omission or conservative retention of equivalent synchronization when observable behavior is preserved.
labels: NoRuntimeSync
-->
`NoRuntimeSync(P)` means that runtime synchronization is not required for correctness of the access.

An implementation MAY omit runtime synchronization for `P`, or MAY conservatively retain equivalent synchronization, provided observable behavior is preserved.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.K-Static-Required
kind: formal-rule
phase: semantic-analysis

owner: spec.key-system

-->
**(K-Static-Required)**
¬ StaticallySafe(P)    ¬ InDynamicContext
──────────────────────────────────────────
Reject
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.6.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.RuntimeSynchronizationRequirements
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires runtime synchronization to enforce key conflict compatibility, block incompatible acquisitions, release keys on scope exit including panic, and guarantee eventual progress under eventual release.
labels: runtime-synchronization, KeyConflict, KeyModeCompatible
-->
When runtime synchronization is required:

1. Mutual exclusion is enforced by `KeyConflict` and `KeyModeCompatible` from §19.3.5.
2. Incompatible acquisitions block until release.
3. Keys are released on scope exit, including panic.
4. Implementations MUST guarantee eventual progress when conflicting holders eventually release.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.DynamicIndexRuntimeOrdering
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires runtime ordering for incomparable dynamic indices inside dynamic contexts to satisfy totality, antisymmetry, transitivity, cross-task consistency, and value-determinism.
labels: dynamic-index-runtime-ordering
-->
Within `#dynamic`, incomparable dynamic indices require a runtime ordering relation satisfying:

1. Totality.
2. Antisymmetry.
3. Transitivity.
4. Cross-task consistency.
5. Value-determinism.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.DynamicIndexedPathCoarsening
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: permitted
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Permits conservative coarsening of non-statically-safe dynamic indexed paths to sound static prefixes that preserve mutual exclusion and observational equivalence.
labels: dynamic-indexed-path-coarsening
-->
An implementation MAY conservatively coarsen a non-statically-safe dynamic indexed path to a static prefix that soundly covers every runtime index reachable by the access.

When such conservative coarsening is used, runtime synchronization is performed on the coarsened path rather than on per-index dynamic keys. This is conforming iff the coarsened path preserves mutual exclusion and observational equivalence.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.CanonicalOrderDeadlockFreedom
kind: metatheoretic-property
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: States deadlock-freedom and eventual acquisition properties under canonical ordering and eventual release.
labels: CanonicalOrder, deadlock-freedom, eventual-acquisition
-->
If all tasks acquire keys in `CanonicalOrder`, no circular wait can occur.

If a task waits for a key and all conflicting holders eventually release, the task eventually acquires the key.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.StaticAndRuntimeKeySafetyEquivalence
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires observable behavior under statically proven key safety and runtime synchronization to be equivalent.
labels: static-runtime-key-safety-equivalence
-->
Observable behavior under statically-proven key safety and under runtime synchronization MUST be observationally equivalent.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.6.6 Lowering

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.K-Dynamic-Permitted
kind: formal-rule
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.lowering, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Emits runtime synchronization for non-statically-safe accesses inside dynamic contexts.
labels: K-Dynamic-Permitted
-->
**(K-Dynamic-Permitted)**
¬ StaticallySafe(P)    InDynamicContext
────────────────────────────────────────
EmitRuntimeSync(P)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.DynamicContextStaticSafeLowering
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: lowering
strength: permitted
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.lowering, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Permits omission or conservative retention of equivalent runtime synchronization when a dynamic-context access is statically safe.
labels: dynamic-context-static-safe-lowering
-->
When `InDynamicContext` and `StaticallySafe(P)` both hold, runtime synchronization is not required. An implementation MAY omit it or conservatively retain equivalent synchronization.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

| `I-CON-0011` | Info     | Compile-time | Runtime synchronization emitted under `#dynamic`      |

### 19.7 Memory Ordering

#### 19.7.1 Syntax

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.19.MemoryOrdering
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.parser, oracle.parser-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines memory-order attributes and fence expression grammar.
labels: memory_order_attribute, memory_order, fence_expr, fence_order
-->
```ebnf
memory_order_attribute ::= attr_open memory_order attr_close
memory_order           ::= "relaxed" | "acquire" | "release" | "acqrel" | "seqcst"
fence_expr             ::= "fence" "(" fence_order ")"
fence_order            ::= "acquire" | "release" | "seqcst"
```
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.7.2 Parsing

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: parse.19.MemoryOrdering
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.parser, oracle.parser-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires memory-order attributes to use generic attribute parsing and fence expressions to be parsed by ordinary expression parsing.
labels: memory-order-attribute-parsing, fence_expr
-->
Memory-order attributes use the generic attribute parser in Chapter 9.

This section defines the surface grammar `fence_expr ::= "fence" "(" fence_order ")"`. No separate named parser helper beyond ordinary expression parsing is introduced here.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.7.3 AST Representation / Form

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: ast.19.MemoryOrderingForms
kind: formal-definition
phase: ast
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.ast, oracle.ast-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines AST representation of memory-order attributes, fence orders, fence expressions, and effective ordering precedence.
labels: FenceOrder, FenceExpr, EffectiveOrdering
-->
Memory-order attributes are attached through the generic attribute forms owned by Chapter 9.
FenceOrder = {`acquire`, `release`, `seqcst`}
Expr = … | FenceExpr(order) | …

EffectiveOrdering(e) is defined by nearest-override precedence:

1. The nearest enclosing expression-level memory-order attribute on `e`.
2. Else the nearest enclosing key-block default memory-order attribute.
3. Else `seqcst`.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.7.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.MemoryOrderingDefaultsAndKeySemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires memory accesses to default to sequential consistency, key acquisition to use acquire semantics, and key release to use release semantics.
labels: memory-order-defaults, key-acquire-ordering, key-release-ordering
-->
Memory accesses default to sequentially consistent ordering.

Key acquisition uses acquire semantics. Key release uses release semantics.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.19.MemoryOrderingLevels
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines ordering levels and their guarantees.
labels: relaxed, acquire, release, acqrel, seqcst
-->
Ordering levels:

| Ordering  | Guarantee                                 |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `relaxed` | Atomicity only; no ordering               |
| `acquire` | Subsequent reads see prior writes         |
| `release` | Prior writes are visible to acquire reads |
| `acqrel`  | Both acquire and release                  |
| `seqcst`  | Total global order                        |
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.MemoryOrderAttributeAttachment
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines valid attachment sites for memory-order attributes and requires at most one such attribute per key block or attributed expression.
labels: memory-order-attribute-attachment
-->
Memory-order attributes MAY be attached to:

1. A key-block statement, establishing a default ordering for keyed or shared accesses in that body.
2. An attributed expression, overriding any enclosing key-block default for that expression subtree.

A key block or attributed expression MUST carry at most one memory-order attribute.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.ExpressionMemoryOrderWellFormedness
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires expression-level memory-order attributes to contain keyed or shared-data access.
labels: expression-memory-order-well-formedness
-->
Expression-level memory-order attributes are well-formed only when the attributed expression contains keyed or shared-data access.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.MemoryOrderDoesNotAlterKeySemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.key-system, compiler.typecheck, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires memory-order attributes to affect only data-access ordering and not alter key acquire or release semantics.
labels: memory-order-key-semantics-invariant
-->
Memory-order attributes affect only data-access ordering. They MUST NOT alter key acquire or key release semantics.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.MemoryOrderNotInsideSpeculativeBlocks
kind: diagnostic-requirement
phase: diagnostics
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.diagnostics, compiler.key-system, oracle.expected-diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires memory-order annotations not to appear inside speculative blocks.
labels: memory-order-speculative-block-restriction, E-CON-0096
-->
Memory-order annotations MUST NOT appear inside speculative blocks.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.T-Fence
kind: formal-rule
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Types fence expressions with valid fence orders as unit.
labels: T-Fence
-->
**(T-Fence)**
O ∈ {`acquire`, `release`, `seqcst`}
────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ `fence`(O) : ()
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.FenceContextAndHeldKeys
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Permits fence operations in runtime expression contexts and requires them not to alter the held-key context.
labels: fence-held-key-context
-->
Fence operations MAY appear in runtime expression contexts. They MUST NOT alter the held-key context.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.7.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.FenceEvaluation
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines fence evaluation as emitting an ordering event and producing unit at the current expression evaluation point.
labels: fence-evaluation, Fence
-->
Evaluation of `fence(O)`:

1. Evaluate `fence(O)` at the current expression evaluation point.
2. Emit ordering event `Fence(O)`.
3. Produce value `()`.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.FenceOrderingConstraints
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines acquire, release, and sequentially consistent fence ordering constraints.
labels: fence-ordering-constraints, acquire, release, seqcst
-->
Required ordering constraints:

1. `fence(acquire)`: operations sequenced after the fence MUST NOT be reordered before it.
2. `fence(release)`: operations sequenced before the fence MUST NOT be reordered after it.
3. `fence(seqcst)`: acquire and release constraints both hold, and all `Fence(seqcst)` events and `#seqcst` accesses participate in one global total order consistent with each task's sequenced-before order.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.19.FenceNoProgramVisibleStorageAccess
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires fence evaluation not to read or write program-visible storage.
labels: fence-no-program-visible-storage-access
-->
Fence evaluation MUST NOT read or write program-visible storage.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.7.6 Lowering

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Lower-Expr-Fence
kind: formal-rule
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.lowering, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Lowers fence expressions to fence IR and unit value.
labels: Lower-Expr-Fence
-->
**(Lower-Expr-Fence)**
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ LowerExpr(FenceExpr(order)) ⇓ ⟨FenceIR(order), UnitVal⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.19.Lower-Ordered-Access
kind: formal-rule
phase: lowering
strength: required
owner: spec.key-system
applies-to: compiler.lowering, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Lowers expressions containing shared access into ordered access IR using the effective ordering.
labels: Lower-Ordered-Access
-->
**(Lower-Ordered-Access)**
ContainsSharedAccess(e)    ord = EffectiveOrdering(e)    Γ ⊢ LowerExprCore(e) ⇓ ⟨IR, v⟩
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ LowerExpr(e) ⇓ ⟨OrderedAccessIR(ord, IR), v⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 19.7.7 Diagnostics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: diagnostics.19.MemoryOrdering
kind: diagnostic-requirement
phase: diagnostics
strength: required

applies-to: compiler.diagnostics, oracle.expected-diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: States that memory ordering introduces no additional named diagnostics beyond the speculative-block restriction owned by speculative execution diagnostics.

No additional named diagnostics are introduced here. The speculative-block restriction on memory-order annotations and fence operations is owned by §19.5.7.

## 20. Structured Parallelism

### 20.1 Parallel Blocks

#### 20.1.1 Syntax

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.20.ParallelBlocks
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.parser, oracle.parser-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines parallel block grammar, including domain expressions, option lists, options, and compile-time dim3 constants.
labels: parallel_block, domain_expr, parallel_option_list, parallel_option, dim3_const, ct_usize_expr
-->
```ebnf
parallel_block       ::= "parallel" domain_expr parallel_option_list? block
domain_expr          ::= expression
parallel_option_list ::= "[" parallel_option ("," parallel_option)* "]"
parallel_option      ::= "cancel" ":" expression
                       | "name" ":" string_literal
                       | "workgroup" ":" dim3_const
                       | "workgroups" ":" dim3_const
dim3_const           ::= "(" ct_usize_expr "," ct_usize_expr "," ct_usize_expr ")"
ct_usize_expr        ::= expression
```
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.1.2 Parsing

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: parse.20.ParallelBlockRules
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.parser, oracle.parser-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires parallel-block parsing to follow named source rules for the domain expression, optional option lists, option list tails, and parallel options.
labels: Parse-Parallel-Expr, Parse-ParallelOptsOpt-None, Parse-ParallelOptsOpt-Yes, Parse-ParallelOptList-Empty, Parse-ParallelOptList-Cons, Parse-ParallelOptListTail-End, Parse-ParallelOptListTail-TrailingComma, Parse-ParallelOptListTail-Comma, Parse-ParallelOpt-Cancel, Parse-ParallelOpt-Name, Parse-ParallelOpt-Workgroup, Parse-ParallelOpt-Workgroups
-->
Parallel-block parsing is defined by the following source rules:

- `Parse-Parallel-Expr`
- `Parse-ParallelOptsOpt-None`
- `Parse-ParallelOptsOpt-Yes`
- `Parse-ParallelOptList-Empty`
- `Parse-ParallelOptList-Cons`
- `Parse-ParallelOptListTail-End`
- `Parse-ParallelOptListTail-TrailingComma`
- `Parse-ParallelOptListTail-Comma`
- `Parse-ParallelOpt-Cancel`
- `Parse-ParallelOpt-Name`
- `Parse-ParallelOpt-Workgroup`
- `Parse-ParallelOpt-Workgroups`

`Parse-Parallel-Expr` parses the domain expression with `ParseExpr_NoBrace`, then parses the optional option list, then parses the block body.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.1.3 AST Representation / Form

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: ast.20.ParallelBlockForms
kind: formal-definition
phase: ast
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.ast, oracle.ast-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines parallel block option forms, option lists, expression form, option resolution judgments, and option-expression extraction.
labels: ParallelOpt, ParallelOpts, ParallelExpr, ResolveParallelOptJudg, ResolveParallelOpt, ResolveParallelOpts, ParallelOptExprs
-->
ParallelOpt = {Cancel(expr), Name(str), Workgroup(dim3), Workgroups(dim3)}

ParallelOpts = [ParallelOpt]

Expr = … | ParallelExpr(domain, opts, body) | …

ResolveParallelOptJudg = {ResolveParallelOpt, ResolveParallelOpts}

ResolveParallelOpt is homomorphic on the option forms:

- If Γ ⊢ ResolveExpr(e) ⇓ e' then Γ ⊢ ResolveParallelOpt(Workgroup(e)) ⇓ Workgroup(e').
- If Γ ⊢ ResolveExpr(e) ⇓ e' then Γ ⊢ ResolveParallelOpt(Workgroups(e)) ⇓ Workgroups(e').

ParallelOptExprs([]) = []

ParallelOptExprs(Cancel(e) :: os) = [e] ++ ParallelOptExprs(os)

ParallelOptExprs(Name(_) :: os) = ParallelOptExprs(os)

ParallelOptExprs(Workgroup(e) :: os) = [e] ++ ParallelOptExprs(os)

ParallelOptExprs(Workgroups(e) :: os) = [e] ++ ParallelOptExprs(os)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.1.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.ParallelBlockOptionValidation
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines parallel block option validation for names, cancellation tokens, compile-time dim3 values, workgroup options, and complete option lists.
labels: BlockOptOk, Dim3Const, BlockOptsOk
-->
BlockOptOk(Name(_)) ⇔ true

BlockOptOk(Cancel(e)) ⇔ G ⊢ e : TypePath(["CancelToken"])

G ⊢ Dim3Const((e_1, e_2, e_3)) ⇓ (x, y, z) ⇔
  G ⊢ e_1 : TypePrim("usize") ∧ G ⊢ ConstLen(e_1) ⇓ x ∧ x > 0 ∧
  G ⊢ e_2 : TypePrim("usize") ∧ G ⊢ ConstLen(e_2) ⇓ y ∧ y > 0 ∧
  G ⊢ e_3 : TypePrim("usize") ∧ G ⊢ ConstLen(e_3) ⇓ z ∧ z > 0

BlockOptOk(Workgroup(e)) ⇔ ∃ dims. G ⊢ Dim3Const(e) ⇓ dims

BlockOptOk(Workgroups(e)) ⇔ ∃ dims. G ⊢ Dim3Const(e) ⇓ dims

BlockOptsOk(opts) ⇔ ∀ opt ∈ opts. BlockOptOk(opt)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.Dim3Const-Err
kind: formal-rule
phase: diagnostics
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.diagnostics, compiler.typecheck, oracle.expected-diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Rejects invalid compile-time dim3 constants.
labels: Dim3Const-Err, E-CON-0159
-->
**(Dim3Const-Err)**
¬∃ dims. G ⊢ Dim3Const(e) ⇓ dims    c = Code(Dim3Const-Err)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Reject
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.ParallelDomainCtorValidation
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines valid parallel domain constructor forms and CPU domain argument requirements.
labels: DomainCtor, DomainCtorOk
-->
DomainCtor(MethodCall(ctx, name, args)) ⇔ name ∈ {`cpu`, `gpu`, `inline`}
DomainCtor(_) ⇔ false
DomainCtorOk(MethodCall(ctx, `cpu`, []))
DomainCtorOk(MethodCall(ctx, `cpu`, [mask])) ⇔ G ⊢ mask : TypePath(["CpuSet"])
DomainCtorOk(MethodCall(ctx, `cpu`, [mask, prio])) ⇔ G ⊢ mask : TypePath(["CpuSet"]) ∧ G ⊢ prio : TypePath(["Priority"])
DomainCtorOk(MethodCall(ctx, `gpu`, []))
DomainCtorOk(MethodCall(ctx, `inline`, []))
DomainCtorOk(D) ⇔ ¬DomainCtor(D)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.T-Parallel
kind: formal-rule
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Types a parallel block when the domain is an ExecutionDomain, constructor and options are valid, and the body typechecks in parallel context.
labels: T-Parallel
-->
**(T-Parallel)**
Γ ⊢ D : `$ExecutionDomain`    DomainCtorOk(D)    BlockOptsOk(opts)    Γ_P = Γ[parallel_context ↦ D]    Γ_P ⊢ B : T
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ `parallel` D opts {B} : T
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.20.ParallelBlockWellFormedness
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires parallel blocks to use ExecutionDomain values, restrict spawn and dispatch to enclosing parallel blocks, and satisfy capture constraints.
labels: parallel-block-well-formedness, E-CON-0101, E-CON-0102
-->
A parallel block is well-formed only if:

1. The domain expression evaluates to a value implementing `ExecutionDomain`.
2. `spawn` and `dispatch` expressions are evaluated only within an enclosing parallel block.
3. Capture constraints from §20.3 are satisfied.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.Parallel-Domain-Param-Err
kind: formal-rule
phase: diagnostics
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.diagnostics, compiler.typecheck, oracle.expected-diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Emits a domain parameter diagnostic when a recognized parallel domain constructor has invalid arguments.
labels: Parallel-Domain-Param-Err, E-CON-0103
-->
**(Parallel-Domain-Param-Err)**
DomainCtor(D)    ¬DomainCtorOk(D)    c = Code(Parallel-Domain-Param-Err)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ `parallel` D opts {B} ⇑ c
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.20.ParallelCancelOptionType
kind: diagnostic-requirement
phase: diagnostics
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.diagnostics, compiler.typecheck, oracle.expected-diagnostics, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires the same rejection form for cancel options whose expression is not a CancelToken.
labels: E-CON-0103, CancelToken
-->
The same rejection form applies when some option `Cancel(e)` is present and Γ ⊢ e : TypePath(["CancelToken"]) does not hold.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.1.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.ParallelState
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines parallel execution state, initialization, and cancel option extraction.
labels: ParallelState, ParallelInit, CancelOpt
-->
ParallelState = {Domain : Value, Handles : List⟨Value⟩, CancelToken : CancelToken@Active | ⊥}

ParallelInit(d, opts) ⇓ pstate ⇔ pstate = {Domain: d, Handles: [], CancelToken: CancelOpt(opts)}

CancelOpt(opts) = token ⇔ Cancel(token) ∈ opts

CancelOpt(opts) = ⊥ ⇔ ∀ opt ∈ opts. opt ≠ Cancel(_)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.ParallelGpuTopologyOptions
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines default GPU workgroup settings, option extraction, and parallel GPU topology computation.
labels: DEFAULT_GPU_WORKGROUP, DEFAULT_GPU_WORKGROUPS, WorkgroupOpt, WorkgroupsOpt, ComputeTopologyParallel
-->
DEFAULT_GPU_WORKGROUP = (64, 1, 1)

DEFAULT_GPU_WORKGROUPS = (1, 1, 1)

WorkgroupOpt(opts) = dims ⇔ Workgroup(dims) ∈ opts

WorkgroupOpt(opts) = ⊥ ⇔ ∀ opt ∈ opts. opt ≠ Workgroup(_)

WorkgroupsOpt(opts) = dims ⇔ Workgroups(dims) ∈ opts

WorkgroupsOpt(opts) = ⊥ ⇔ ∀ opt ∈ opts. opt ≠ Workgroups(_)

ComputeTopologyParallel(opts) = topo ⇔
  wg = if WorkgroupOpt(opts) ≠ ⊥ then WorkgroupOpt(opts) else DEFAULT_GPU_WORKGROUP ∧
  ng = if WorkgroupsOpt(opts) ≠ ⊥ then WorkgroupsOpt(opts) else DEFAULT_GPU_WORKGROUPS ∧
  topo = ⟨
    WorkgroupSize := wg,
    NumWorkgroups := ng,
    GlobalSize := (wg.0 × ng.0, wg.1 × ng.1, wg.2 × ng.2)
  ⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.AwaitSpawned
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines awaiting spawned handles and selecting the failed completion with least completion-sequence number.
labels: AwaitSpawned
-->
AwaitSpawned(pstate, σ) ⇓ (panic_opt, σ') ⇔ every handle in `pstate.Handles` reaches `Ready` or `Failed` between `σ` and `σ'`, and `panic_opt` is the failed completion associated with the least completion-sequence number among handles in `pstate.Handles` whose terminal state is `Failed`, or `⊥` if none fail.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.EvalSigma-Parallel
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Evaluates a parallel expression by evaluating its domain, initializing parallel state, evaluating the body in parallel context, awaiting spawned handles, and returning the body value.
labels: EvalSigma-Parallel
-->
**(EvalSigma-Parallel)**
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(D, σ) ⇓ (Val(d), σ_1)    ParallelInit(d, opts) ⇓ pstate_0    topology = if IsGpuDomain(d) then ComputeTopologyParallel(opts) else ⊥    Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(B, σ_1[parallel_context ↦ pstate_0]) ⇓ (Val(v_body), σ_2)    LookupVal(σ_2, parallel_context) = pstate_n    AwaitSpawned(pstate_n, σ_2) ⇓ (⊥, σ_3)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(ParallelExpr(D, opts, B), σ) ⇓ (Val(v_body), σ_3)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.EvalSigma-Parallel-Body-Ctrl
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage

labels: EvalSigma-Parallel-Body-Ctrl
-->
**(EvalSigma-Parallel-Body-Ctrl)**
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(D, σ) ⇓ (Val(d), σ_1)    ParallelInit(d, opts) ⇓ pstate_0    Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(B, σ_1[parallel_context ↦ pstate_0]) ⇓ (Ctrl(κ), σ_2)    LookupVal(σ_2, parallel_context) = pstate_n    AwaitSpawned(pstate_n, σ_2) ⇓ (⊥, σ_3)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(ParallelExpr(D, opts, B), σ) ⇓ (Ctrl(κ), σ_3)

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.DispatchGpuTopologyComputation
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines GPU topology computation for dispatch bounds and options.
labels: ComputeTopologyDispatch, WorkgroupOpt, DEFAULT_GPU_WORKGROUP, CeilDiv
-->
ComputeTopologyDispatch(bounds, opts) = topo ⇔
  wg = if WorkgroupOpt(opts) ≠ ⊥ then WorkgroupOpt(opts) else DEFAULT_GPU_WORKGROUP ∧
  volume = wg.0 × wg.1 × wg.2 ∧
  groups = CeilDiv(|bounds|, volume) ∧
  topo = ⟨
    WorkgroupSize := wg,
    NumWorkgroups := (groups, 1, 1),
    GlobalSize := (wg.0 × groups, wg.1, wg.2)
  ⟩
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

**GPU Execution Topology.** Work-items are organized into a 3-dimensional hierarchy of workgroups.

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.GpuExecutionTopology
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines GPU topology dimensions, work item and workgroup identifiers, and global identifier computation.
labels: GpuTopology, WorkItemId, WorkgroupId, GlobalId
-->
GpuTopology = ⟨GlobalSize, WorkgroupSize, NumWorkgroups⟩
GlobalSize : (usize, usize, usize)
WorkgroupSize : (usize, usize, usize)
NumWorkgroups : (usize, usize, usize)

WorkItemId = (usize, usize, usize)
WorkgroupId = (usize, usize, usize)
GlobalId(local_id, workgroup_id, workgroup_size) =
  (local_id.0 + workgroup_id.0 × workgroup_size.0,
   local_id.1 + workgroup_id.1 × workgroup_size.1,
   local_id.2 + workgroup_id.2 × workgroup_size.2)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

  ⟨`gpu_num_workgroups`, [], TypeTuple([TypePrim("usize"), TypePrim("usize"), TypePrim("usize")])⟩,

  ⟨`gpu_barrier`, [], TypePrim("()")⟩,
  ⟨`gpu_memory_barrier`, [], TypePrim("()")⟩,

}

GpuIntrinsicNames = {name | ⟨name, _, _⟩ ∈ GpuIntrinsicTable}

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.GpuRuntimeState
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines GPU runtime state, workgroup state, work item state, status values, barrier predicate, and 3D-linear ID conversion helpers.
labels: GpuState, WorkgroupState, GpuWorkItem, GpuWorkItemStatus, AtBarrier, LinearId, LocalIdFromLinear
-->
GpuState = ⟨Topology, GlobalMem, WorkgroupStates⟩

WorkgroupState = ⟨SharedMem, WorkItems, BarrierCount⟩

GpuWorkItem = ⟨id, local_id, workgroup_id, expr, captures, status, private_mem⟩

GpuWorkItemStatus = {Pending, Running, AtBarrier, Done}
AtBarrier(wi) ⇔ wi.status = AtBarrier
LinearId(id_3d, size) = id_3d.0 + id_3d.1 × size.0 + id_3d.2 × size.0 × size.1
LocalIdFromLinear(linear, workgroup_size) = (
  linear % workgroup_size.0,
  (linear / workgroup_size.0) % workgroup_size.1,
  linear / (workgroup_size.0 × workgroup_size.1)
)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.2.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.20.ExecutionDomainContextMethods
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines Context execution-domain methods and their selected execution domains.
labels: ctx.cpu, ctx.gpu, ctx.inline, ExecutionDomain, CpuSet, Priority
-->
`ctx.cpu()`, `ctx.gpu()`, and `ctx.inline()` are `Context` methods that each return a value of type `$ExecutionDomain`.

`ctx.cpu()` selects the domain-default CPU execution domain.

`ctx.cpu(mask)` selects a CPU execution domain restricted to the `CpuSet` mask.

`ctx.cpu(mask, priority)` selects a CPU execution domain restricted to the `CpuSet` mask and default task `Priority`.

`ctx.gpu()` selects the default GPU execution domain.

`ctx.inline()` selects the inline execution domain.

`CpuSet` is an alias of `u64` interpreted as a CPU-bitset mask.

`Priority` is an enum with variants `Low`, `Normal`, and `High`.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.GpuSafeType
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines GpuSafeType in terms of prohibited GPU types and GPU-safe components.
labels: GpuSafeType, ProhibitedGpuType, GpuSafeComponents, GpuSafePrimTypes
-->
`GpuSafeType(T)` holds iff `¬ProhibitedGpuType(T)` and `GpuSafeComponents(T)`.
GpuSafeType(T) ⇔ ¬ProhibitedGpuType(T) ∧ GpuSafeComponents(T)

GpuSafePrimTypes = {`i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `isize`, `usize`, `f16`, `f32`, `f64`, `bool`, `()`}

ProhibitedGpuType(T) ⇔
  T = TypeDynamic(_) ∨
  T = TypePath(["Context"]) ∨
  IsCapabilityType(T) ∨
  T = TypeString(`@Managed`) ∨
  T = TypeBytes(`@Managed`) ∨
  T = TypePtr(_, `@Valid`) ∨
  T = TypeModalState(_, _) ∨
  ModalRefType(T)

GpuSafeComponents(T) ⇔ BitcopyType(T) ∧ (CompoundType(T) ⇒ ∀ elem ∈ Elements(T). GpuSafeType(elem))
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.GpuSafePredicateClauses
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines generic predicate requirements for type parameters used by GPU-safe compound types.
labels: HasGpuSafeReq, GpuSafePredicateClauseOk, GpuSafe
-->
HasGpuSafeReq(W, x) ⇔ ∃ wp ∈ PredicateReqs(W). wp = PredicateReq(`GpuSafe`, TypePath([x]))

GpuSafePredicateClauseOk(params, W) ⇔ ∀ p ∈ params. (p.name ∈ TypeParamsUsed ⇒ HasGpuSafeReq(W, p.name))
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.2.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.20.InlineDomainSemantics
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines inline-domain runtime semantics for spawn, dispatch, actual parallelism, and retained capture and permission rules.
labels: inline-domain-semantics
-->
Inline-domain semantics:

1. `spawn { e }` evaluates `e` immediately and blocks until completion.
2. `dispatch i in range { e }` executes as a sequential loop.
3. No actual parallelism occurs.
4. Capture and permission rules remain enforced.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

summary: Defines GPU memory visibility for global, shared, and private address spaces.
labels: GpuMemVisible
-->
GpuMemVisible(addr, S, wg, wi) ⇔
  (S = Global) ∨
  (S = Shared ∧ WorkgroupOf(wi) = wg) ∨
  (S = Private ∧ wi = CurrentWorkItem)

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.GpuTopologyValidity
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines valid GPU topology and maximum workgroup size.
labels: TopologyValid, MAX_WORKGROUP_SIZE
-->
TopologyValid(topo) ⇔
  topo.WorkgroupSize.0 > 0 ∧ topo.WorkgroupSize.1 > 0 ∧ topo.WorkgroupSize.2 > 0 ∧
  topo.WorkgroupSize.0 × topo.WorkgroupSize.1 × topo.WorkgroupSize.2 ≤ MAX_WORKGROUP_SIZE ∧
  topo.GlobalSize.0 = topo.WorkgroupSize.0 × topo.NumWorkgroups.0 ∧
  topo.GlobalSize.1 = topo.WorkgroupSize.1 × topo.NumWorkgroups.1 ∧
  topo.GlobalSize.2 = topo.WorkgroupSize.2 × topo.NumWorkgroups.2

MAX_WORKGROUP_SIZE = 1024
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism

summary: Requires GPU barrier waiting until all work-items in the workgroup reach the barrier and makes shared-memory writes visible after completion.
labels: GpuBarrierWait, gpu_barrier
-->
GpuBarrierWait(wg) blocks execution until all work-items in workgroup wg reach the barrier.

`gpu_barrier()` blocks until all work-items in the workgroup reach the barrier. After barrier completion, all shared-memory writes by work-items in that workgroup are visible to all work-items in that workgroup.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

labels: GpuCaptureJudg, GpuCaptureOk, HasHeapProvenance
-->
GpuCaptureJudg = {GpuCaptureOk(Γ, x, T)}

HasHeapProvenance(Γ, x) ⇔ Γ[x].provenance = π_Heap ∨ (Γ[x].provenance = π_Derived(y) ∧ HasHeapProvenance(Γ, y))

#### 20.3.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.20.ParallelCapturePermissions
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines capture permission policy for const, shared, and unique bindings in spawn and dispatch bodies.
labels: parallel-capture-permissions, E-CON-0120
-->
Bindings with `const` permission MAY be captured by reference into `spawn` and `dispatch` bodies.

Bindings with `shared` permission MAY be captured by reference into `spawn` and `dispatch` bodies. Access synchronization is defined by Chapter 19.

Bindings with `unique` permission MUST NOT be captured by closures used in `spawn` or `dispatch` bodies.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

summary: Accepts const captures in closures used for spawn or dispatch bodies.
labels: Parallel-Closure-Capture-Const
-->
**(Parallel-Closure-Capture-Const)**
C = ClosureExpr(params, ret_type_opt, body)    Context(C) ⊆ {SpawnBody, DispatchBody}    x ∈ ConstCaptures(C)

spawn_expr         ::= "spawn" spawn_option_list? block

#### 20.4.3 AST Representation / Form

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: ast.20.SpawnForms
kind: formal-definition
phase: ast
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.ast, oracle.ast-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines spawn option forms, option lists, expression form, option resolution judgments, option-expression extraction, Spawned states, and the built-in Spawned reference.
labels: SpawnOpt, SpawnOpts, SpawnExpr, ResolveSpawnOptJudg, ResolveSpawnOpt, ResolveSpawnOpts, SpawnOptExprs, Spawned
-->
SpawnOpt = {Name(str), Affinity(expr), Priority(expr)}

SpawnOpts = [SpawnOpt]

Expr = … | SpawnExpr(opts, body) | …

ResolveSpawnOptJudg = {ResolveSpawnOpt, ResolveSpawnOpts}

SpawnOptExprs([]) = []

SpawnOptExprs(Name(_) :: os) = SpawnOptExprs(os)

SpawnOptExprs(Affinity(e) :: os) = [e] ++ SpawnOptExprs(os)

SpawnOptExprs(Priority(e) :: os) = [e] ++ SpawnOptExprs(os)

States(`Spawned`) = { `@Pending`, `@Ready` }

See §13.1.4 for the built-in `Spawned<T>` modal declaration, state set, payload, and type registration.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.4.4 Static Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

labels: SpawnOptOk, SpawnOptsOk, CpuSet, Priority
-->
SpawnOptOk(Name(_)) ⇔ true

SpawnOptOk(Affinity(e)) ⇔ Γ ⊢ e : TypePath(["CpuSet"])

SpawnOptOk(Priority(e)) ⇔ Γ ⊢ e : TypePath(["Priority"])

SpawnOptsOk(opts) ⇔ ∀ opt ∈ opts. SpawnOptOk(opt)

**(T-Spawn)**

<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.4.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.SpawnHandleAndEnqueue
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines spawn handles, captured environments, and enqueueing work into a parallel state.
labels: SpawnHandle, CapturedEnv, EnqueueWork
-->
SpawnHandle = {id : ℕ, state : Pending | Ready(Value) | Failed(Panic)}

CapturedEnv(e, σ) = { x ↦ LookupVal(σ, x) | x ∈ FreeVars(e) }

EnqueueWork(pstate, w, opts) ⇓ pstate' ⇔ pstate' = pstate[Handles := pstate.Handles ++ [SpawnedVal(@Pending, w.id)]] and work item `w` is submitted to `pstate.Domain` subject to `opts`
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: requirement.20.SpawnEvaluationProcedure
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines spawn evaluation steps, affinity behavior, priority scheduling obligation, work enqueueing, and immediate pending handle return.
labels: spawn-evaluation, affinity, priority, Spawned
-->
Evaluation of `spawn [opts] { e }`:

1. Capture free variables per §20.3.
2. Package the captured environment and body into a work item.
3. If `affinity` is present, restrict worker selection to CPU indices whose bits are set in the `CpuSet` mask; if the set is empty, use the domain default.
4. If `priority` is present, assign the task the given `Priority`. When multiple tasks are ready, workers MUST select any task of maximal priority among those ready.
5. Enqueue the work item.
6. Return `Spawned<T>@Pending` immediately.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.EvalSigma-Spawn
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Evaluates a spawn expression by capturing the environment, creating a pending work item, enqueueing it, and returning a pending Spawned handle.
labels: EvalSigma-Spawn
-->
**(EvalSigma-Spawn)**
Γ[parallel_context] = pstate    caps = CapturedEnv(e, σ)    w = {id: NextWorkId(pstate), expr: e, captures: caps, status: Pending}    EnqueueWork(pstate, w, opts) ⇓ pstate'    handle = SpawnedVal(@Pending, w.id)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(SpawnExpr(opts, e), σ) ⇓ (Val(handle), σ[parallel_context ↦ pstate'])
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires Spawned handle result retrieval to be defined by asynchronous operation semantics.
labels: Spawned
-->
Result retrieval for `Spawned<T>` handles is defined by §21.2.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

### 20.5 Dispatch

#### 20.5.1 Syntax

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: grammar.20.Dispatch
kind: grammar
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.parser, oracle.parser-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines dispatch expression grammar, key clauses, dispatch options, and reduction operators.
labels: dispatch_expr, key_clause, key_mode, dispatch_option_list, dispatch_option, reduce_op
-->
```ebnf
dispatch_expr         ::= "dispatch" pattern "in" range_expression key_clause? dispatch_option_list? block
key_clause            ::= "key" key_path_expr key_mode
key_mode              ::= "read" | "write"
dispatch_option_list  ::= "[" dispatch_option ("," dispatch_option)* "]"
dispatch_option       ::= "reduce" ":" reduce_op
                        | "ordered"
                        | "chunk" ":" expression
                        | "workgroup" ":" dim3_const
reduce_op             ::= "+" | "*" | "min" | "max" | "and" | "or" | identifier
```
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.5.2 Parsing

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: parse.20.DispatchRules
kind: semantic-requirement
phase: parsing
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.parser, oracle.parser-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Requires dispatch parsing to follow named source rules for dispatch expressions, key clauses, option lists, reduction operators, and dispatch options.
labels: Parse-Dispatch-Expr, Parse-KeyClauseOpt-None, Parse-KeyClauseOpt-Yes, Parse-DispatchOptsOpt-None, Parse-DispatchOptsOpt-Yes, Parse-DispatchOptList-Empty, Parse-DispatchOptList-Cons, Parse-DispatchOptListTail-End, Parse-DispatchOptListTail-TrailingComma, Parse-DispatchOptListTail-Comma, Parse-ReduceOp-Op, Parse-ReduceOp-Ident, Parse-DispatchOpt-Reduce, Parse-DispatchOpt-Ordered, Parse-DispatchOpt-Chunk, Parse-DispatchOpt-Workgroup
-->
Dispatch parsing is defined by the following source rules:

- `Parse-Dispatch-Expr`
- `Parse-KeyClauseOpt-None`
- `Parse-KeyClauseOpt-Yes`
- `Parse-DispatchOptsOpt-None`
- `Parse-DispatchOptsOpt-Yes`
- `Parse-DispatchOptList-Empty`
- `Parse-DispatchOptList-Cons`
- `Parse-DispatchOptListTail-End`
- `Parse-DispatchOptListTail-TrailingComma`
- `Parse-DispatchOptListTail-Comma`
- `Parse-ReduceOp-Op`
- `Parse-ReduceOp-Ident`
- `Parse-DispatchOpt-Reduce`
- `Parse-DispatchOpt-Ordered`
- `Parse-DispatchOpt-Chunk`
- `Parse-DispatchOpt-Workgroup`

The fixed identifiers `min`, `max`, `and`, and `or` are tokenized as identifiers by Chapter 4 and are accepted in dispatch position by `Parse-ReduceOp-Ident`.
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

#### 20.5.3 AST Representation / Form

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: ast.20.DispatchForms
kind: formal-definition
phase: ast
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.ast, oracle.ast-fixtures, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines dispatch reduction operators, option forms, key clauses, dispatch expression form, resolution judgments, option expression extraction, and access set forms.
labels: ReduceOp, DispatchOpt, DispatchOpts, KeyClause, KeyClauseOpt, DispatchExpr, ResolveKeyClauseJudg, ResolveDispatchOptJudg, DispatchOptExprs, DispatchAccess, DispatchAccessSet
-->
ReduceOp = {`+`, `*`, `min`, `max`, `and`, `or`} ∪ Identifier

DispatchOpt = {Reduce(op), Ordered, Chunk(expr), Workgroup(dim3)}    op ∈ ReduceOp

DispatchOpts = [DispatchOpt]

KeyClause = ⟨path, mode⟩

KeyClauseOpt = {⊥} ∪ KeyClause

Expr = … | DispatchExpr(pat, range, key_clause_opt, opts, body) | …

ResolveKeyClauseJudg = {ResolveKeyClauseOpt}

ResolveDispatchOptJudg = {ResolveDispatchOpt, ResolveDispatchOpts}

DispatchOptExprs([]) = []

DispatchOptExprs(Reduce(_) :: os) = DispatchOptExprs(os)

DispatchOptExprs(Ordered :: os) = DispatchOptExprs(os)

DispatchOptExprs(Chunk(e) :: os) = [e] ++ DispatchOptExprs(os)

DispatchOptExprs(Workgroup(e) :: os) = [e] ++ DispatchOptExprs(os)

DispatchAccess = ⟨schema, mode⟩    mode ∈ {Read, Write}

DispatchAccessSet = [DispatchAccess]
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.DispatchAccessInference
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.key-system, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines dispatch pattern variables, path roots, dispatch invariance, implicit dispatch uses, schemas, mode joining, access merging, and inferred dispatch accesses.
labels: DispatchPatternVars, PathRootVar, DispatchInvariant, InsideKeyBlock, ImplicitDispatchUse, SchemaOf, JoinDispatchMode, MergeDispatchAccesses, InferDispatchAccesses
-->
DispatchPatternVars(pat) = PatNames(pat)

PathRootVar(expr) = x ⇔ KeyPath(expr) is rooted at binding `x`

DispatchInvariant(expr, pat) ⇔ FreeVars(expr) \ {PathRootVar(expr)} ⊆ DispatchPatternVars(pat) ∪ { x | x ∈ dom(Γ) ∧ Γ[x] = TypePerm(`const`, _) }

InsideKeyBlock(B, e) ⇔ ∃ K. K is a key block in `B` and `e` is a proper subexpression of `K.body`

ImplicitDispatchUse(B, e) ⇔
  e ∈ Subexpressions(B) ∧
  ¬InsideKeyBlock(B, e) ∧
  (∃ T. Γ ⊢ e : TypePerm(`shared`, T) ∨ Γ ⊢ e :place TypePerm(`shared`, T)) ∧
  KeyPath(e) is defined ∧
  RequiredMode(e) is defined

SchemaOf(pat, e) = S ⇔ S is `KeyPath(e)` with occurrences of bindings in `DispatchPatternVars(pat)` left symbolic and all other subexpressions preserved

JoinDispatchMode(Read, Read) = Read

JoinDispatchMode(_, _) = Write

MergeDispatchAccesses(raw) = merged where `merged` contains one entry per distinct schema and the mode for each schema is the join of all modes attached to that schema in `raw`

InferDispatchAccesses(pat, B) = merged ⇔
  raw = [⟨SchemaOf(pat, e), RequiredMode(e)⟩ | e ∈ Subexpressions(B) ∧ ImplicitDispatchUse(B, e) ∧ DispatchInvariant(KeyPath(e), pat)] ∧
  MergeDispatchAccesses(raw) = merged
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.DispatchOptionsAndDynamicKeys
kind: formal-definition
phase: semantic-analysis
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: compiler.typecheck, compiler.key-system, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines chunk option extraction, associative built-in reductions, dispatch-static index expressions, and dynamic key pattern detection.
labels: ChunkExpr, AssociativeReduce, DispatchStaticIndexExpr, DynamicKeyPattern
-->
ChunkExpr(opts) = e ⇔ Chunk(e) ∈ opts
ChunkExpr(opts) = ⊥ ⇔ ∀ o ∈ opts. o ≠ Chunk(_)
AssociativeReduce(`+`) ⇔ true
AssociativeReduce(`*`) ⇔ true
AssociativeReduce(`min`) ⇔ true
AssociativeReduce(`max`) ⇔ true
AssociativeReduce(`and`) ⇔ true
AssociativeReduce(`or`) ⇔ true
AssociativeReduce(_) ⇔ false
DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e) ⇔
  e is a compile-time constant expression ∨
  (e = x ∧ x ∈ DispatchPatternVars(pat)) ∨
  (e = e_0.f ∧ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e_0)) ∨
  (e = e_0.n ∧ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e_0)) ∨
  (e = e_0[e_1] ∧ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e_0) ∧ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e_1)) ∨
  (e = op e_0 ∧ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e_0)) ∨
  (e = e_0 op e_1 ∧ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e_0) ∧ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e_1)) ∨
  (e = cast(e_0, _) ∧ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e_0))
DynamicKeyPattern(pat, spec) ⇔ ∃ ⟨S, _⟩ ∈ spec. S contains an index expression e ∧ ¬ DispatchStaticIndexExpr(pat, e)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.Dispatch-Infer-Err
kind: formal-rule
phase: diagnostics
strength: required

summary: Rejects implicit dispatch shared accesses whose key path is not invariant under the dispatch pattern.
labels: Dispatch-Infer-Err, E-CON-0141
-->
**(Dispatch-Infer-Err)**

Reject

#### 20.5.5 Dynamic Semantics

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.DispatchPartitionSpec
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines dispatch partition specs from explicit key clauses or inferred accesses.
labels: DispatchPartitionSpec, InferDispatchAccesses, ModeOf
-->
DispatchPartitionSpec(pat, key_clause, B) = [⟨SchemaOf(pat, key_e), ModeOf(key_clause)⟩] ⇔ key_clause = `key` key_e mode

DispatchPartitionSpec(pat, ⊥, B) = ks ⇔ InferDispatchAccesses(pat, B) = ks
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.DispatchIndexAndPathDisjointness
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines schema instantiation, index normalization and equivalence, affine dispatch indices, index disjointness, path disjointness, prefix equality, segment equality, and segment disjointness.
labels: InstantiateSchema, IdxNorm, idx-equivalence, AffineDispatchIndex, ProvablyDisjoint, ProvablyDisjointPath, PrefixEqThrough, SegEqForDispatch, SegmentProvablyDisjoint
-->
InstantiateSchema(S, v) = P ⇔ `P` is obtained by substituting `v` for the dispatch-pattern bindings in `S`

IdxNorm(e) is `e` with harmless parentheses and expression attributes removed

e₁ ≡_idx e₂ ⇔ IdxNorm(e₁) and IdxNorm(e₂) are syntactically identical

AffineDispatchIndex(e) = ⟨x, k⟩ ⇔
  (e = x ∧ k = 0) ∨
  (e = x + n ∧ n is a compile-time constant integer expression with value k) ∨
  (e = x - n ∧ n is a compile-time constant integer expression with value n₀ ∧ k = -n₀) ∨
  (e = n + x ∧ n is a compile-time constant integer expression with value k)

ProvablyDisjoint(e₁, e₂) ⇔
  (e₁ and e₂ are distinct integer literals) ∨
  (AffineDispatchIndex(e₁) = ⟨x, k₁⟩ ∧ AffineDispatchIndex(e₂) = ⟨x, k₂⟩ ∧ k₁ ≠ k₂)

ProvablyDisjointPath(P, Q) ⇔ ∃ k. PrefixEqThrough(P, Q, k-1) ∧ SegmentProvablyDisjoint(P[k], Q[k])
PrefixEqThrough(P, Q, 0) ⇔ true
PrefixEqThrough(P, Q, k) ⇔ ∀ r ∈ 1..k. SegEqForDispatch(P[r], Q[r])

SegEqForDispatch(Root(x), Root(y)) ⇔ x = y

SegEqForDispatch(Field(_, f), Field(_, g)) ⇔ f = g

SegEqForDispatch(Index(_, e_1), Index(_, e_2)) ⇔ e_1 ≡_idx e_2

SegmentProvablyDisjoint(Root(x), Root(y)) ⇔ x ≠ y

SegmentProvablyDisjoint(Field(_, f), Field(_, g)) ⇔ f ≠ g

SegmentProvablyDisjoint(Index(_, e_1), Index(_, e_2)) ⇔ ProvablyDisjoint(e_1, e_2)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.DispatchPartitioning
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.key-system, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines dispatch partitioning by key conflicts, connected components, ordered groups, and total iteration count.
labels: PartitionByKey, DispatchPartition, TotalIterations, Conflict, ConnectedComponents, OrderedByLeastMember
-->
PartitionByKey(range, key_spec) = [Group_1, …, Group_k] ⇔
  IterBounds(range) = (start, end) ∧
  indices = [start, start+1, …, end-1] ∧
  Conflict(i, j) ⇔ i ≠ j ∧ (∃ ⟨S_a, M_a⟩ ∈ key_spec, ⟨S_b, M_b⟩ ∈ key_spec. P_i = InstantiateSchema(S_a, i) ∧ P_j = InstantiateSchema(S_b, j) ∧ ¬ ProvablyDisjointPath(P_i, P_j) ∧ ¬ KeyModeCompatible(M_a, M_b)) ∧
  ConnectedComponents(indices, Conflict) = [Group_1, …, Group_k] ∧
  OrderedByLeastMember([Group_1, …, Group_k])

DispatchPartition(pat, range, key_clause, B) = [Group_1, …, Group_k] ⇔ DispatchPartitionSpec(pat, key_clause, B) = key_spec ∧ PartitionByKey(range, key_spec) = [Group_1, …, Group_k]
TotalIterations([Group_1, …, Group_k]) = Σ_{i=1..k} |Group_i|
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.DispatchReductionAndChunking
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines reduction option extraction, chunk size evaluation, contiguous chunk construction, and chunk group construction.
labels: ReduceOpOf, ChunkSizeOf, ContiguousChunks, ChunkGroups
-->
ReduceOpOf(attrs) = op ⇔ Reduce(op) ∈ attrs

ReduceOpOf(attrs) = ⊥ ⇔ ∀ a ∈ attrs. a ≠ Reduce(_)

ChunkSizeOf(attrs, σ) ⇓ (n, σ') ⇔ ChunkExpr(attrs) = ⊥ ∧ n = 1 ∧ σ' = σ
ChunkSizeOf(attrs, σ) ⇓ (n, σ_1) ⇔ ChunkExpr(attrs) = e ∧ Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(e, σ) ⇓ (Val(IntVal("usize", n)), σ_1) ∧ n > 0

ContiguousChunks([], n) = []
ContiguousChunks([i_1, …, i_k], n) = [[i_1, …, i_m]] ++ ContiguousChunks([i_{m+1}, …, i_k], n) where m = min(n, k)
ChunkGroups(groups, n) = concat([ContiguousChunks(G, n) | G ∈ groups])
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.EvalSigma-Dispatch
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism

summary: Evaluates dispatch by evaluating the range, computing chunk size, partitioning, chunking groups, selecting reduction, running dispatch, and returning the result.
labels: EvalSigma-Dispatch
-->
**(EvalSigma-Dispatch)**
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(range, σ) ⇓ (Val(r), σ_1)    ChunkSizeOf(attrs, σ_1) ⇓ (n, σ_2)    DispatchPartition(pat, r, key_opt, B) = groups_0    groups = ChunkGroups(groups_0, n)    ReduceOpOf(attrs) = reduce_opt    Γ ⊢ DispatchRun(pat, B, groups, reduce_opt, σ_2) ⇓ (out, σ_3)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(DispatchExpr(pat, range, key_opt, attrs, B), σ) ⇓ (out, σ_3)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT

labels: EvalSigma-Dispatch-Range-Ctrl
-->
**(EvalSigma-Dispatch-Range-Ctrl)**
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(range, σ) ⇓ (Ctrl(κ), σ_1)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(DispatchExpr(pat, range, key_opt, attrs, B), σ) ⇓ (Ctrl(κ), σ_1)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: rule.20.EvalSigma-Dispatch-Chunk-Ctrl
kind: formal-rule
phase: runtime

-->

Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(range, σ) ⇓ (Val(r), σ_1)    ChunkExpr(attrs) = e    Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(e, σ_1) ⇓ (Ctrl(κ), σ_2)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ EvalSigma(DispatchExpr(pat, range, key_opt, attrs, B), σ) ⇓ (Ctrl(κ), σ_2)
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

<!-- ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT
id: def.20.DispatchRun
kind: formal-definition
phase: runtime
strength: required
owner: spec.structured-parallelism
applies-to: runtime.evaluator, compiler.parallelism, oracle.reference-model, oracle.coverage
summary: Defines dispatch run outcomes for non-reducing completion, reducing completion, panic propagation, and reduced empty iteration-space panic.
labels: DispatchRun, P-SEM-2862
-->
DispatchRun(pat, B, groups, ⊥, σ) ⇓ (Val(()), σ') ⇔ all groups execute to completion without panic and every iteration result is discarded

DispatchRun(pat, B, groups, op, σ) ⇓ (Val(v), σ') ⇔ all groups execute to completion without panic and `v` is the deterministic reduction of all iteration results under `op`

DispatchRun(pat, B, groups, reduce_opt, σ) ⇓ (Ctrl(Panic), σ') ⇔ some iteration panics and all started iterations settle before panic propagation

DispatchRun(pat, B, groups, op, σ) ⇓ (Ctrl(Panic), σ) ⇔ op ≠ ⊥ ∧ TotalIterations(groups) = 0
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->

| ------------ | -------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `E-CON-0140` | Error    | Compile-time | Dispatch outside parallel block               |
| `E-CON-0141` | Error    | Compile-time | Key inference failed; explicit key required   |
| `E-CON-0142` | Error    | Compile-time | Cross-iteration dependency detected           |
| `E-CON-0143` | Error    | Compile-time | Non-associative reduction without `[ordered]` |
| `W-CON-0140` | Warning  | Compile-time | Dynamic key pattern; runtime serialization    |
<!-- /ULTRAVIOLET-SPEC-UNIT -->
